Accountable obligation owner.value: Group Controller owns the Solvency II internal-control-over-financial-reporting matrix for every undertaking inside the Art. 212(1)(c) group scope; escalation to the Chief Financial Officer

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Solvency II Directive 2009/138/EC Art. 246(1)-(2) and Art. 47(1)-(2) plus Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Arts. 258-260 and 271(3), re-read against the consolidated EUR-Lex text at each annual refresh, including the amendments made by Directive (EU) 2025/2

In-scope processes.value: Solvency II balance-sheet close for every solo undertaking and the group: economic valuation of assets, technical provisions handover from Actuarial, own funds tiering, SCR/MCR assembly, QRT production (S.02.01, S.23.01, S.25.01, S.32.01) and SFCR/RSR narrative — including subsidiaries and SPVs not individually subject to Solvency II

In-scope systems.value: Group consolidation ledger feeding the Solvency II balance sheet, with the general ledger, the actuarial reserving platform and the asset system as upstream sources; control matrix held in the GRC platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: Group Solvency II ICFR Procedure — entity-level and process-level control matrix, one row per control with risk, assertion, frequency, preventive/detective type, owner, evidence artefact and the Art. 246/271(3) linkage for each in-scope undertaking

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and noted by the Audit Committee at the pre-year-end sitting; re-approved annually and on any change of group scope, EIOPA taxonomy release or acquisition

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Control matrix must be refreshed and re-certified before the hard close: solo annual reporting is due 14 weeks after the financial year end and group annual reporting 20 weeks, so ICFR sign-off is set at year-end + 8 weeks to leave review runway

Deadline reminders configured.value: Close calendar tasks at year-end minus 60 days (matrix refresh), minus 30 days (control owner re-certification) and year-end plus 8 weeks (ICFR sign-off), each with an owner and an escalation to the Controller after 5 days overdue

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Control matrix versions, control-owner certifications, walkthrough notes and remediation records retained 10 years from the reporting reference date to cover the supervisory review period under Art. 36

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every control failure, unmapped subsidiary and unremediated design gap is raised as a deficiency record with severity (deficiency / significant deficiency / material weakness), root cause, owner and target date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CFO signs the annual ICFR conclusion and every material-weakness remediation closure; the Chief Risk Officer countersigns where the deficiency touches the SCR

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All key controls in the group Solvency II ICFR matrix across every undertaking in the scope of group supervision, plus the full list of Art. 212 group entities reconciled to template S.32.01 as filed

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Any in-scope undertaking with no mapped control set is an automatic fail; any key control failing design or operating effectiveness with a balance-sheet impact above 0.5% of group eligible own funds is a significant deficiency; two or more aggregating above 1% is a material weakness

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous with an annual re-certification; testing is annual over the full matrix with interim design walkthroughs at Q3 for any newly acquired or newly consolidated undertaking

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Finance and must not own or perform any control in the tested matrix

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual group ICFR testing file (entity scoping memo, matrix extract, walkthrough notes, test sheets, deficiency log) in the compliance evidence repository under the reporting reference date

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Control matrix export, scoping memo showing every S.32.01 entity mapped, and the deficiency register — presentable to the group supervisor or the college of supervisors within 10 business days of an Art. 35 information request

Regulator response path.value: The Regulatory Reporting Manager owns correspondence with the group supervisor; the Chief Financial Officer clears any answer that concedes a control weakness, and the Corporate Secretary logs it for the Audit Committee

checklist.step: Fix the group supervision perimeter for the reporting year
actions: Pull the legal-entity register from the consolidation tool and list every participation, subsidiary, SPV, ancillary services undertaking and third-country undertaking with the group holding percentage.
Ask the Corporate Secretary for the year's share transactions, new incorporations and liquidations and add or remove entities accordingly.
Tag each entity as solo Solvency II undertaking, non-Solvency II undertaking inside Art. 212(1)(c) group scope, or out of scope, and write the Art. 212/213 basis in a Reason column.
Reconcile the resulting list line for line to template S.32.01 (Undertakings in the scope of the group) as it will be filed and clear every difference with the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Have the Chief Financial Officer approve the scoping memo before any control mapping starts.
checklist.done: the scoping memo lists every group entity with an Art. 212 basis and ties exactly to S.32.01.

checklist.step: Rebase the control matrix on the Solvency II balance-sheet processes
actions: In the GRC platform open the Solvency II ICFR matrix and confirm one process row exists for each of: economic valuation of assets, technical provisions handover, reinsurance recoverables, deferred tax, own funds tiering, SCR/MCR assembly and QRT production.

For each process record the financial-statement assertion at risk (existence, valuation, completeness, presentation) and the QRT template it feeds (S.02.01, S.12.01/S.17.01, S.23.01, S.25.01, S.28.01).
Delete controls that reference retired systems and flag any process with no preventive control as a design gap.
Set the matrix version number and record the EIOPA taxonomy release the QRT controls were written against.
checklist.done: every Solvency II balance-sheet process has at least one preventive and one detective control mapped to an assertion and a QRT template.

checklist.step: Push consistent control standards into the non-Solvency II subsidiaries
actions: Send each in-scope non-Solvency II subsidiary the group minimum control set (valuation review, data completeness reconciliation, journal approval, intragroup elimination, reporting-package certification) required by Art. 246(2).
Hold a working call with each local finance lead to map the group control id to whatever local control already exists, or to raise an implementation action where none does.
Record proportionality decisions on the matrix row with a written justification — never leave a subsidiary row blank because it is small.
Collect a signed local adoption confirmation from each subsidiary finance lead and store it against the entity in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: each in-scope non-Solvency II subsidiary has the group minimum control set mapped or an owned implementation action, with a signed adoption confirmation.

checklist.step: Document the data flow from source systems into the Solvency II balance sheet
actions: Trace each Solvency II balance-sheet line back through the consolidation tool to its source: general ledger account, asset system position file, actuarial reserving output or reinsurance ledger.
Register in the data catalog, for each feed, the extract job, the cut-off timestamp, the transformation applied and the owner of the source.
Set completeness, accuracy and appropriateness checks per Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 19 on each feed — record count, control total, currency and valuation date agreement.
Flag any manual spreadsheet in the chain and attach a compensating review control naming the reviewer.
checklist.done: every Solvency II balance-sheet line has a documented lineage with named source owner, cut-off and data-quality checks.

checklist.step: Test the technical provisions handover control between Actuarial and Finance
actions: Take the signed technical provisions delivery pack from the Appointed Actuary — best estimate and risk margin, gross and net of reinsurance, by line of business and by currency.
Reconcile the pack totals to what was posted into the consolidation tool for S.12.01 (life) and S.17.01 (non-life) and prove the difference is nil or fully explained by an approved late adjustment.
Confirm the delivery pack carries the actuarial sign-off name, date and model version before any posting is allowed.
Record the reconciliation on the control evidence sheet with both preparer and reviewer initials.
checklist.done: posted technical provisions agree to the signed actuarial delivery pack with a nil or fully explained difference.

checklist.step: Control the intragroup eliminations and the group own funds build
actions: Run the intragroup transaction report in the consolidation tool and match each intragroup loan, reinsurance treaty, guarantee and dividend to its counterparty entity booking.
Clear unmatched pairs with the local finance leads before the group balance sheet is locked, and carry the cleared list to templates S.36.01 to S.36.04.
Recalculate group eligible own funds after eliminating intragroup creation of capital, and check tiering limits under Art. 82 of the Delegated Regulation.
Attach the elimination workbook and the tiering check to the control row as evidence.
checklist.done: intragroup transactions are fully matched, eliminated and reflected in the S.36 templates, and own funds tiering limits are evidenced.

checklist.step: Establish the review control over the SCR and MCR assembly
actions: Take the standard-formula module outputs (market, counterparty default, life, health, non-life underwriting, operational) and check each feeds the correlation aggregation with the correct sign and correct currency.
Re-run the loss-absorbing capacity of deferred tax adjustment and confirm it is supported by the deferred tax recoverability memo from Tax.
Reconcile the assembled SCR to templates S.25.01 and the MCR to S.28.01, including the MCR floor and cap at 25%/45% of SCR under Art. 129.
Have a second actuary who did not run the calculation initial the reconciliation before it is released to Finance.
checklist.done: SCR and MCR tie to S.25.01 and S.28.01 with the MCR corridor tested and a second-actuary initial on the reconciliation.

checklist.step: Run the entity-level control assessment for governance consistency
actions: Confirm each in-scope undertaking has the four key functions (risk management, compliance, internal audit, actuarial) allocated with a named holder and a fit-and-proper record per Art. 42.
Check where a function is discharged group-wide under Art. 246(4) that the group policy names the local point of contact and the escalation path.
Confirm the group written policies (risk management, internal control, internal audit, outsourcing) were adopted locally by each subsidiary board and record the adoption date.
Raise a deficiency where a subsidiary board has adopted an older policy version than the one currently in force.
checklist.done: every in-scope undertaking shows named key-function holders and a dated local adoption of the current group policies.

checklist.step: Certify controls with their owners before the close
actions: Issue the certification campaign from the GRC platform to every control owner at year-end minus 30 days.
Require each owner to confirm the control description still matches what they do, name the evidence artefact and its storage location, and declare any known failure in the period.
Chase non-responders at day 5 and day 10, then escalate the remaining names to the Controller.
Lock the matrix version once certifications close and record the completion percentage.
checklist.done: 100% of control owners have certified or been escalated, and the matrix version is locked.

checklist.step: Walk through each key control and collect operating evidence
actions: For each key control take one occurrence and follow it end to end with the performer, recording what they opened, what they compared and what they did on a difference.
Collect the actual artefact — the signed reconciliation, the system approval screenshot with user id and timestamp, the reviewed exception report — not a description of it.
Check the evidence proves review, not just preparation: an initial with no supporting comparison is a design gap.
File each walkthrough note against the control row with the date and the performer name.
checklist.done: every key control has a dated walkthrough note and a real operating artefact attached.

checklist.step: Grade deficiencies and quantify their balance-sheet effect
actions: List every failed or missing control and quantify the potential misstatement in eligible own funds and in the SCR ratio.
Grade each as deficiency, significant deficiency or material weakness against the 0.5%/1% of eligible own funds thresholds.
Aggregate deficiencies that touch the same balance-sheet line before grading, so several small ones cannot hide a material one.
Take the grading to the Chief Financial Officer for challenge and record any change of grade with its reason.
checklist.done: every deficiency is quantified, graded, aggregated by balance-sheet line and challenged by the CFO.

checklist.step: Open remediation plans with owners and dates
actions: Raise a remediation record per deficiency with the root cause, the redesigned control, the owner and a target date inside the next reporting cycle.
For any deficiency affecting a subsidiary, name both the local owner and the group finance sponsor so it cannot stall at the local entity.
Add an interim compensating control where the redesigned control will not be live before the next close, and evidence it separately.
Report open remediations to the Audit Committee monthly until closed.
checklist.done: every deficiency has a remediation record with root cause, owner, date and either a live fix or an evidenced compensating control.

checklist.step: Draft the system-of-governance narrative for the SFCR and RSR
actions: Draft SFCR section B (System of Governance) covering the internal control system, the four key functions and how group-wide consistency is achieved under Art. 246.
Cross-check each statement in the narrative against the control matrix and the entity-level assessment — no statement without a matrix row behind it.
Note any material change of governance in the year and the date the board approved it.
Under Directive (EU) 2025/2 keep the policyholder part and the professional part of the SFCR aligned so the governance description is not contradicted between the two.
checklist.done: the SFCR/RSR governance narrative is drafted and every assertion is traceable to a control matrix row or a board record.

checklist.step: Take the ICFR conclusion to the Audit Committee and the board
actions: Publish to the board portal the ICFR conclusion pack: scoping memo, matrix coverage statistics, deficiency register with grades and the remediation plan.
Present at the Audit Committee the entities where group standards are applied proportionately and explain why that remains consistent with Art. 246(2).
Obtain the committee's conclusion in the minutes and the board's approval of the system-of-governance description before the SFCR is signed.
Record the minute reference on the ICFR conclusion memo.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee has concluded and the board has approved, with the minute reference recorded on the conclusion memo.

checklist.step: Archive the ICFR file for the supervisory retention period
actions: Move the locked matrix version, certifications, walkthrough notes, deficiency register, board minute extract and scoping memo into the evidence repository under the reporting reference date.
Apply the 10-year retention label and restrict edit rights so the filed version cannot be altered after sign-off.
Check the repository index makes the file searchable by legal entity, control id and reporting reference date.
Send the Regulatory Reporting Manager the repository link so it can be quoted in any Art. 35 supervisory request.
checklist.done: the ICFR file is archived read-only with a 10-year label and is retrievable by entity, control id and reference date.

testing.step: Rebuild the population of in-scope undertakings and key controls
actions: Export from the GRC platform every control flagged key in the Solvency II ICFR matrix, with entity, process, assertion, owner and frequency.
Export the group legal-entity register from the consolidation tool independently of the Controller's scoping memo.
Reconcile both to the filed S.32.01 entity list and record the three-way count difference before doing anything else.
Sign the population as complete only once every S.32.01 entity appears in the control matrix or has a documented out-of-scope basis.
testing.done: the control population reconciles three ways to S.32.01 and is signed complete.

testing.step: Test that no in-scope entity is left without the group minimum control set
actions: Pivot the control population by entity and list every entity with fewer than the five group minimum controls required by Art. 246(2).
For each shortfall read the recorded proportionality justification and test whether it names a real risk assessment rather than entity size alone.
Confirm the signed local adoption confirmation exists and post-dates the current group policy version.
Log every entity with no control set as an automatic fail regardless of materiality.
testing.done: each in-scope entity either carries the minimum control set or a justification tested against a documented risk assessment.

testing.step: Draw a reproducible sample of key controls
actions: Take 100% of controls over technical provisions handover, own funds tiering and SCR assembly.
Take 25 further controls by seeded random selection across the remaining population, weighted to entities acquired or consolidated in the year, minimum 45 controls in total.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Have the Chief Audit Executive approve the sampling plan before fieldwork starts.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, covers all valuation-critical controls and is approved.

testing.step: Re-perform the technical provisions handover reconciliation
actions: Take the Appointed Actuary's signed technical provisions delivery pack directly from Actuarial, not the copy filed by Finance.
Re-add best estimate and risk margin by line of business and by currency and compare to the amounts posted into the consolidation tool and reported at S.12.01 and S.17.01.
Investigate every difference above 0.1% of the line-of-business best estimate and trace it to an approved late adjustment with a named approver.
Screenshot both the delivery pack totals and the posted trial balance into the workpaper.
testing.done: posted technical provisions are independently re-added and agree to the signed pack within the 0.1% investigation threshold.

testing.step: Recompute own funds tiering and the MCR corridor
actions: Recalculate eligible own funds by tier from the S.23.01 detail and apply the quantitative limits in Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 82 to the SCR and to the MCR separately.
Recompute the MCR from the linear MCR and confirm it sits between 25% and 45% of the SCR and above the absolute floor in Art. 129(1)(d).
Confirm intragroup capital creation has been eliminated by tracing three intragroup capital instruments to their eliminations.
Any breach of a tiering limit or the MCR corridor is reported as a breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: own funds tiering and the MCR corridor are independently recomputed and agree to S.23.01 and S.28.01.

testing.step: Trace sampled controls to real operating evidence
actions: For each sampled control obtain the artefact for the tested occurrence and confirm it carries a performer identity, a date and the comparison actually made.
Reject evidence that is only an initial, an email saying done, or a screenshot with no user id or timestamp.
Check the evidence date falls inside the control frequency window — a monthly control evidenced twice a year fails operating effectiveness.
Record pass/fail per control with the artefact reference in the test sheet.
testing.done: each sampled control has a dated, attributable artefact inside its frequency window or is marked failed.

testing.step: Verify key-function allocation and fit-and-proper records
actions: For 10 sampled undertakings confirm named holders of the risk management, compliance, internal audit and actuarial functions under Art. 42 and Art. 44-48.
Confirm the fit-and-proper file holds the competence assessment, the propriety check and the notification to the supervisor where local law requires one.
Where a function is discharged at group level, confirm the group policy names the local contact and the escalation route, and that internal audit remains independent under Art. 47(2).
Flag any combination of functions that compromises internal audit independence as a governance breach.
testing.done: all four key functions are evidenced for every sampled undertaking with intact internal audit independence.

testing.step: Test data lineage and cut-off on the Solvency II balance sheet
actions: Select five balance-sheet lines and re-trace each from S.02.01 back through the consolidation tool to the source extract.
Compare the recorded extract cut-off timestamp to the reporting reference date and prove no post-cut-off movement was included.
Re-run the Art. 19 completeness and accuracy checks on the source extracts and compare the control totals to those retained by Finance.
List every manual spreadsheet in the chain and test that its compensating review control was actually performed.
testing.done: all five traced lines reconcile source to S.02.01 with cut-off proven and manual steps compensated.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, grading and owner
actions: Raise an audit issue per exception recording the entity, control id, what failed, and the quantified effect on eligible own funds and the SCR ratio.
Assign a root cause (entity outside the matrix, stale control description, evidence not retained, proportionality misused) and a named owner with a date.
Compare your grading to the Controller's deficiency register and report any control graded lower by management than by audit.
Carry every open issue into next year's testing as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue record, quantified effect, root cause, owner, date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the control failure rate and compare it to the 0.5%/1% eligible own funds severity thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — naming the evidence references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who owns and performs no control in the matrix, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and every significant deficiency to the Audit Committee before the SFCR governance section is signed, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with a stated conclusion, failure rate and a dated Audit Committee reporting reference.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Chief Audit Executive owns the annual test of key controls over the actuarial function's contribution to risk management, SCR/MCR modelling and the ORSA; escalation to the Audit Committee chair

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Solvency II Directive 2009/138/EC Art. 48(1)(g), (h) and (i) read with Art. 45 (ORSA) and Art. 47 (internal audit), plus Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Arts. 269-272; verified against the consolidated EUR-Lex text at audit planning

In-scope processes.value: Actuarial function inputs to the risk management system: technical provisions feeding the SCR standard formula, underwriting policy opinion, reinsurance adequacy opinion, risk modelling assumptions and the ORSA quantitative sections

In-scope systems.value: Reserving and capital models with their assumption sets and run logs, the model governance repository holding versions and validations, and the ORSA workbook

Compliance procedure documented.value: Annual Internal Audit Programme for the Actuarial Function — risk assessment, key control inventory over model change, assumption setting, data quality and ORSA input, sampling approach and deficiency grading

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Audit Committee as part of the annual audit plan; re-approved on any material model change, internal model application or ORSA methodology change

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Fieldwork must complete before the Actuarial Function Report is tabled to the board and before the RSR is due, so testing closes at year-end plus 10 weeks against the 14-week solo and 20-week group annual reporting deadlines; the ORSA supervisory report is due within 2 weeks of ORSA completion

Deadline reminders configured.value: Audit plan milestones at planning (year-end minus 8 weeks), fieldwork start (year-end plus 2 weeks), draft report (plus 8 weeks), committee tabling (plus 10 weeks), each alerting the Chief Audit Executive on slippage

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Audit programme, test sheets, model run extracts, assumption approval records and the issued report retained 10 years from the audit report date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Each control failure is an audit issue graded high/medium/low with root cause, quantified SCR effect where measurable, owner and agreed remediation date, tracked to closure with evidence

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CRO accepts closure of every high-graded issue affecting risk modelling or the ORSA; the Chief Actuary confirms the model or assumption fix is in production

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All model changes, assumption changes and expert-judgement decisions applied to the reserving and SCR models during the financial year, plus every ORSA stress and scenario run in the ORSA cycle

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Any model change put into production without recorded validation and approval is a fail; any expert judgement with no documented rationale is a fail; more than 5% of sampled changes failing, or any single failure moving the SCR ratio by more than 2 percentage points, escalates to the Audit Committee

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous with an annual actuarial function report; audit testing is annual, with an interim review whenever a major model change or an out-of-cycle ORSA is triggered under Art. 45(1)

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Second-line reviewer independent of Actuarial and of Internal Audit fieldwork, who performed none of the sampled model runs or validations

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual actuarial function audit file (programme, risk assessment, sample rationale, re-performance evidence, issue log, report) in the compliance evidence repository indexed by audit year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Issued audit report, issue log with closure evidence and the Audit Committee minute, packaged for the supervisor within 10 business days of an Art. 35 request or a supervisory review process meeting

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Risk Officer fronts supervisory questions on risk modelling; the Chief Audit Executive answers questions on audit scope and independence; the Head of Compliance logs every supervisory interaction

checklist.step: Build the annual risk assessment over the actuarial function
actions: Interview the Chief Actuary, the Chief Risk Officer and the Head of Capital Management on what changed in the year: models, assumptions, reinsurance structure, product mix and data sources.
Score each actuarial process for inherent risk against SCR sensitivity and prior-year issues, and rank them.
Set the audit scope explicitly against Art. 48(1)(g), (h) and (i) so the report can be cited in the supervisory dialogue.
Table the scope to the Audit Committee for approval and record the minute reference.
checklist.done: a scored risk assessment and an Audit Committee-approved scope citing Art. 48(1)(g)-(i) exist.

checklist.step: Inventory the key controls over model change and assumption setting
actions: Extract from the model governance repository the control inventory covering model change request, independent validation, approval authority, production release and post-implementation review.
Add the assumption-setting controls: annual experience study, assumption committee approval, expert-judgement documentation and back-testing.
Confirm each control names an owner, a frequency and an evidence artefact; raise a design gap where the artefact is not named.
Agree the inventory in writing with the Chief Actuary before fieldwork.
checklist.done: an agreed control inventory covers model change, validation, approval, release and assumption setting with named evidence artefacts.

checklist.step: Extract the population of model and assumption changes in the year
actions: Pull the model version history and run log from the actuarial platform for the reserving and SCR models covering the full financial year.
Pull the assumption change register (mortality, lapse, expense, claims inflation, discount curve selection, loss ratio picks) with effective dates.
Reconcile both extracts to the change requests recorded in the model governance repository and resolve every unmatched item before sampling.
Have the extract signed as complete by the Chief Actuary.
checklist.done: the change population reconciles between the platform run log and the governance repository and is signed complete.

checklist.step: Sample model changes and re-perform the validation check
actions: Take 100% of changes flagged major and 20 minor changes by seeded random selection, recording the seed and population size.
For each sampled change open the validation report and confirm it was written by someone outside the development team, dated before the production release.
Re-run the validation test where it is reproducible — a benchmark model, a closed-form check or a prior-period rerun — and compare to the recorded result.
Mark as a fail any change released before its validation date, even where the validation later concluded satisfactory.
checklist.done: each sampled model change has an independent, pre-release validation and a re-performed or reconciled test result.

checklist.step: Test the documentation behind every expert judgement
actions: List the expert judgements applied in the year: assumption overlays, IBNR loadings, data adjustments, ENID allowances and contract boundary calls.
For each, read the rationale and check it names the evidence considered, the alternatives rejected, the materiality and the approver, as required by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 2.
Test whether the judgement was reviewed for continuing appropriateness at the next valuation date.
Fail any judgement documented only as prior-year approach retained.
checklist.done: every expert judgement carries evidence, alternatives, materiality, approver and a continuing-appropriateness review.

checklist.step: Test data quality controls feeding the models
actions: Take the data directory required by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 19 and confirm it lists each data set used, its source, its owner and its update cycle.
Re-run the completeness, accuracy and appropriateness checks on the policy, claims and asset extracts and compare record counts and control totals to those retained by Actuarial.
Test the treatment of data gaps: confirm the adjustment method is documented and the adjusted volume is quantified.
Fail any extract whose control totals cannot be reproduced from the warehouse.
checklist.done: the Art. 19 data directory is complete and every sampled extract's control totals are independently reproduced.

checklist.step: Audit the actuarial function's contribution to the ORSA
actions: Take the ORSA report and list each quantitative input supplied by the actuarial function: projected technical provisions, projected SCR, stress and scenario results and the overall solvency needs figure.
Trace each input back to a dated model run in the platform run log and confirm the run version matches the version cited in the ORSA.
Confirm the actuarial function's written input to the ORSA exists and that the board challenged it, evidenced in the ORSA committee or board minutes.
Confirm the ORSA supervisory report was submitted to the national competent authority within 2 weeks of the board approving the ORSA.
checklist.done: every ORSA quantitative input traces to a versioned model run, with evidenced board challenge and a timely supervisory submission.

checklist.step: Test the underwriting policy opinion under Art. 48(1)(g)
actions: Obtain the actuarial function's written opinion on the overall underwriting policy for the year and confirm it addresses sufficiency of premiums, expected new-business profitability and the effect of inflation and anti-selection.

Confirm sustainability risks were taken into account as required by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 272(6a) inserted by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/1256, and that the opinion names the sustainability factors considered.
Trace the opinion to the underwriting committee or board minute where it was received and challenged.
Fail an opinion that restates the policy without expressing a conclusion.
checklist.done: the underwriting policy opinion states a conclusion, covers sustainability risks and is minuted as received by the board.

checklist.step: Test the reinsurance adequacy opinion under Art. 48(1)(h)
actions: Pull the in-force treaty schedule from the treaty repository with retentions, limits, reinstatements and reinsurer identity for the year.
Confirm the actuarial opinion tests the programme against the company's risk appetite, the modelled 1-in-200 gross loss and the counterparty default risk module inputs.
Confirm the opinion covers the credit quality of reinsurers and the effect of the programme on the SCR, not just its cost.
Trace the opinion to its delivery to the administrative, management or supervisory body.
checklist.done: the reinsurance opinion tests the actual in-force programme against risk appetite and counterparty quality and was delivered to the AMSB.

checklist.step: Re-perform selected SCR module calculations
actions: Rebuild independently in a controlled workbook two standard-formula sub-modules — typically interest rate and lapse — from the underlying exposure data.
Apply the shocks in Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Arts. 165-181 and the correlation matrices in Annex IV and compare to the reported S.26 template values.
Investigate any difference above 1% of the module capital charge and trace it to a documented model choice.
Attach the rebuild workbook, its inputs and the comparison to the audit file.
checklist.done: two SCR sub-modules are independently rebuilt and agree to the S.26 templates within the 1% investigation threshold.

checklist.step: Check the actuarial function's independence and resourcing
actions: Confirm the actuarial function holder meets the fit-and-proper requirement of Art. 42 and that the appointment was notified to the supervisor where local law requires it.
Check the function's reporting line reaches the board without going through the business it opines on, per Art. 48(2).
Compare headcount and skills to the model and product complexity and record any resourcing gap flagged by the Chief Actuary in the year.
Confirm no individual both sets an assumption and validates it.
checklist.done: independence, fitness, reporting line and segregation of setting from validating are all evidenced.

checklist.step: Grade findings and quantify the capital effect
actions: Grade each finding high, medium or low against the effect on the SCR ratio, on the technical provisions, and on the reliability of the ORSA.
Quantify, with Capital Management, the SCR ratio movement for any finding that would change a reported figure, in percentage points.
Escalate immediately, without waiting for the report, any finding that would move the SCR ratio by more than 2 percentage points.
Record the grading rationale on each issue so it survives challenge.
checklist.done: every finding is graded with a quantified SCR effect and severe findings are escalated on discovery.

checklist.step: Agree remediation with the Chief Actuary and the CRO
actions: Hold the closing meeting with the Chief Actuary and agree an action, an owner and a date for every finding.
Require model or assumption fixes to be scheduled against a named valuation date so they cannot drift across reporting cycles.
Where a fix cannot land before the next valuation, agree a documented interim overlay and the disclosure treatment with the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Record management responses verbatim in the report, including any acceptance of risk with its rationale.
checklist.done: every finding has an agreed action, owner, valuation-dated deadline and a recorded management response.

checklist.step: Issue the report and table it to the Audit Committee
actions: Issue the audit report with the scope wording tied to Art. 48(1)(g)-(i), the opinion, the findings and the agreed actions.
Publish it to the board portal ahead of the Audit Committee and present the high-graded findings in person.
Confirm the Actuarial Function Report tabled to the board reflects any finding that changes a stated conclusion.
Record the committee minute reference on the report cover.
checklist.done: the report is issued, tabled and minuted, and the Actuarial Function Report reflects the findings.

checklist.step: Track issues to evidenced closure and archive the file
actions: Chase each open issue at its due date and require closure evidence — the validation report, the released model version number, the updated assumption paper.
Reject closure claimed on a plan rather than a delivered change and reopen the issue with a new date.
Report overdue issues to the Audit Committee at every sitting until closed.
Archive the audit file in the evidence repository under the audit year with a 10-year retention label.
checklist.done: every issue is closed on delivered evidence or reported overdue, and the audit file is archived for 10 years.

testing.step: Rebuild the population of model and assumption changes independently
actions: Export the model change register and the assumption change register from the model governance repository for the financial year.
Export the model run log and version history directly from the actuarial platform without going through Actuarial.
Reconcile the two counts and list every platform version with no governance record — those are the highest-risk rows.
Sign the population as complete and record the extraction date and query used.
testing.done: the change population is independently rebuilt, reconciled to the platform run log and signed complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the audit sample back to the population
actions: Re-draw the sample using the seed and stratification recorded in the audit workpaper and compare item for item to the sample actually tested.
Confirm 100% coverage of major changes was genuinely achieved by checking the major/minor flag on every population row.
Investigate any change reclassified from major to minor during the year and the approver of that reclassification.
Log any sample that cannot be reproduced as a testing-quality exception.
testing.done: the tested sample reproduces exactly from the recorded seed and all major changes are covered.

testing.step: Re-perform an independent validation on two sampled model changes
actions: Select two sampled changes with the largest technical provision impact and re-run the pre-change and post-change model versions on the same data set.
Compare the movement produced to the movement claimed in the change request and in the analysis of change.
Confirm the validator named on the report reports outside the model development team, using the HR reporting line, not a job title.
Capture both run identifiers and the comparison into the workpaper.
testing.done: two changes are independently re-run, the movement reconciles to the analysis of change, and validator independence is proven on the reporting line.

testing.step: Recompute the SCR effect of the tested changes
actions: Take the reported SCR from S.25.01 and the technical provisions from S.12.01/S.17.01 before and after each sampled change.
Recompute the SCR ratio movement in percentage points and compare it to the figure recorded on the audit issue.
Check that any change moving the ratio by more than 2 percentage points was escalated on discovery, not at report issue.
Any unescalated breach of the escalation trigger is an exception against the audit process itself.
testing.done: SCR ratio movements are recomputed, agree to the issue records and the escalation trigger is proven to have operated.

testing.step: Test the ORSA input trail end to end
actions: Pick three ORSA scenarios and trace each stated result to a dated, versioned run in the actuarial platform run log.
Confirm the run version cited in the ORSA equals the version actually executed, not a later rebuild.
Read the board or ORSA committee minute and confirm the challenge is recorded with substance, not merely noted.
Confirm the ORSA supervisory report submission date is within 2 weeks of board approval and capture the submission receipt.
testing.done: all three scenarios trace to versioned runs, board challenge is minuted with substance and the 2-week submission is evidenced.

testing.step: Re-read the two Art. 48 opinions against the underlying facts
actions: Re-read the reinsurance adequacy opinion beside the in-force treaty schedule and confirm every material treaty in force at the reference date is covered.
Confirm the retention and limit figures quoted in the opinion match the treaty repository, and that reinsurer credit quality feeds the counterparty default module.
Re-read the underwriting policy opinion and confirm the sustainability considerations required by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 272(6a) are actually named, not asserted.
Log a wrong-facts opinion as a fail even where the conclusion happens to be reasonable.
testing.done: both opinions are re-read against source records with figures and sustainability factors verified.

testing.step: Test expert judgement documentation on a fresh sub-sample
actions: Draw eight expert judgements independently of the audit sample, weighted to the largest reserve overlays.
Confirm each records evidence considered, alternatives rejected, quantified materiality and a named approver with authority.
Confirm the judgement was re-assessed at the following valuation date with a written continuing-appropriateness conclusion.
Compare your pass/fail to the auditor's for any judgement in both samples and report divergence.
testing.done: eight independently drawn judgements are tested and any divergence from the auditor's conclusion is reported.

testing.step: Test data quality reproduction on the valuation extracts
actions: Re-run the policy and claims extracts from the warehouse at the valuation cut-off and compare record counts, sums insured and paid/incurred totals to the actuarial data pack.
Test the documented treatment of missing data by recomputing the adjusted volume and comparing to the value used in the models.
Confirm the Art. 19 data directory names an owner for every data set and that the owner still holds the role.
Any control total that cannot be reproduced is an exception, regardless of size.
testing.done: extract control totals are reproduced from the warehouse and data-gap adjustments are recomputed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the model or assumption, what failed, and the quantified technical provision or SCR effect.
Assign a root cause (validation after release, undocumented judgement, unreproducible data, stale ORSA version) and an owner with a valuation-dated deadline.
Flag any issue that repeats a prior-year finding as a repeat and escalate it a grade.
Carry every open exception into the next annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, quantified effect, owner, deadline and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the committee
actions: Compute the sampled failure rate and compare it to the 5% threshold and the 2 percentage point SCR trigger.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the evidence references behind each element.
Have the independent reviewer, who ran none of the sampled model runs or validations, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee before the Actuarial Function Report is finalised and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, failure rate and committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

checklist.step: Open the engagement file and record the rotation clocks
actions: Create the engagement file for the financial year holding the audit firm name, the engagement letter, the key audit partner and the engagement quality control reviewer.

Record the first financial year the firm was appointed for each EU insurance undertaking and compute the consecutive years served against the 10-year maximum in Art. 17(1) of Regulation (EU) 537/2014.
Record the first year the key audit partner signed and compute the years served against the 7-year maximum in Art. 17(7), plus the 3-year cooling-off.
Publish the clocks to the board portal so the Audit Committee sees the years remaining at every sitting.
checklist.done: the engagement file shows firm and partner start years, years served and years remaining for every EU insurance undertaking.

checklist.step: Obtain and read the annual independence confirmation
actions: Request from the audit firm the written independence confirmation required by Art. 6(2)(a) of Regulation (EU) 537/2014, covering the firm, its network and the engagement team.
Check the letter names every threat identified — self-review, self-interest, advocacy, familiarity, intimidation — and the safeguard applied to each, not just a blanket confirmation.
Confirm the letter covers all group entities in the audit scope, including third-country subsidiaries served by network firms.
File the signed letter to the board portal and calendar the pre-signing re-confirmation.
checklist.done: a signed independence letter naming threats and safeguards is on file for the firm, network and engagement team.

checklist.step: Confirm each audit team member's personal independence declarations
actions: Ask the audit firm for the list of the engagement team and confirm each has completed the firm's personal independence declaration for the period.

Cross-check the team list against the group's employee register for anyone who joined the company from the audit firm within the last 12 months, and against the board and key function holder list for the Art. 22a cooling-off rule.
Check no team member holds a financial interest in the company or an entity in the group.
Record any match as a threat and require the firm to state the safeguard or replace the individual.
checklist.done: no engagement team member breaches the financial interest or cooling-off rules, or a documented safeguard is on file.

checklist.step: Maintain the prohibited and permitted non-audit service lists
actions: Take the prohibited service list in Art. 5(1) of Regulation (EU) 537/2014 — tax services affecting the financial statements, bookkeeping, payroll, internal audit outsourcing, valuation, legal services, HR services for key management — and record the member state additions and derogations that apply to each undertaking.
Publish the list to Procurement and to every budget holder who can raise a purchase order against the audit firm.
Block the audit firm's supplier record in the procurement system so no purchase order can be raised without a compliance release.
Refresh the list annually and on any national implementing change.
checklist.done: an up-to-date jurisdiction-specific prohibited service list is published and the auditor's supplier record is gated.

checklist.step: Pre-approve every non-audit service before work starts
actions: Require a written request per proposed engagement naming the service, the entity, the fee, the personnel and the reason the audit firm is being used.
Assess it against the prohibited list and the threat analysis required by Art. 5(4), and record the safeguards proposed.
Route it to the Audit Committee for prior approval — chair's approval only within the delegated threshold recorded in the policy, and reported to the next full committee.
Record the decision, date and approver in the pre-approval register and release the purchase order only against a register reference.
checklist.done: no non-audit engagement starts without a dated pre-approval register entry and a released purchase order reference.

checklist.step: Compute the non-audit fee cap each quarter
actions: Extract from the general ledger and accounts payable every invoice from the audit firm and its network firms for the year, by entity and by service description.
Split the spend into statutory audit fees, services required by EU or national law, and other permitted non-audit services.

Compute the Art. 4(2) cap: total non-audit fees against 70% of the average statutory audit fees of the last three consecutive financial years, at the audited entity, its parent, its controlled undertakings and the consolidated level.
Report the ratio to the Audit Committee each quarter with the projected year-end position and freeze new engagements once it passes 55%.
checklist.done: the fee cap ratio is computed from ledger data at every required level and reported quarterly with a projected year-end position.

checklist.step: Test the rotation clocks against tender lead time
actions: Compare each firm rotation date to today plus the tender lead time recorded in the policy (12 months as the working assumption for an Art. 16 selection procedure).

Where the 10-year term is being extended, confirm the public tender under Art. 16(2)-(5) was actually run and documented, or that a joint audit is in place for the 24-year option, and that the member state permits the extension used.
Confirm the key audit partner replacement is named and briefed at least one audit cycle before the 7-year date.
Escalate any date that cannot be met to the Audit Committee chair within one business day.
checklist.done: every rotation date is either met, covered by a documented tender or extension basis, or escalated to the committee chair.

checklist.step: Run the auditor selection procedure where rotation falls due
actions: Prepare tender documents that state the selection criteria in advance and do not restrict participation to firms with a given prior-year fee share, per Art. 16(3).
Invite firms, evaluate against the stated criteria, and record the evaluation scoring for each.
Have the Audit Committee produce a recommendation with at least two options and a justified preference, per Art. 16(2).
Take the recommendation to the board and then to the general meeting for appointment, and retain the full tender file.
checklist.done: a documented tender produced a two-option committee recommendation with a justified preference and a general meeting appointment.

checklist.step: Read the auditor's additional report to the Audit Committee
actions: Obtain the additional report required by Art. 11 of Regulation (EU) 537/2014 before the audit report is signed.
Check it declares independence, describes the methodology, states materiality and quantitative levels, and lists significant deficiencies in internal financial control.
Map every deficiency it raises to the group ICFR deficiency register so nothing sits only in the auditor's report.
Table the report at the Audit Committee and record the discussion in the minutes.
checklist.done: the Art. 11 additional report is received before the audit opinion, its deficiencies are mapped to the ICFR register and it is minuted.

checklist.step: Confirm the audit scope covers the SFCR where national law requires it
actions: Check for each undertaking whether the national competent authority requires external audit of the SFCR balance sheet and own funds sections.
Where required, confirm the engagement letter names the SFCR sections in scope and the reporting deadline aligned to the 14-week solo publication date.
Agree with the auditor the templates in scope, typically S.02.01, S.23.01 and S.25.01, and the assurance standard applied.
Record the scope decision and its national law basis in the engagement file.
checklist.done: SFCR audit scope is confirmed per undertaking with the national basis and the templates named in the engagement letter.

checklist.step: Re-confirm independence immediately before the opinion is signed
actions: Send the audit firm a request to re-confirm independence covering the whole period from engagement to signing date.
Attach the year's pre-approval register and ask the firm to confirm it matches its own engagement records, and to explain any difference.
Have the Audit Committee record its own conclusion on independence in the minutes, as required by Art. 6(2)(c).
Withhold the audit committee's recommendation to sign until both confirmations are on file.
checklist.done: a re-confirmation reconciled to the pre-approval register and a minuted committee conclusion exist before signing.

checklist.step: Assess and treat any independence breach
actions: Where a prohibited service, unapproved engagement, fee cap breach or missed rotation is found, record the facts, the dates and the entities affected.
Assess under Art. 5 and Art. 17 whether the breach affects the auditor's ability to hold office and whether the audit report must be reconsidered.
Decide the notification path — audit oversight authority, insurance supervisor, or both — and the deadline for each, and record the reasoning.
Agree the safeguard or remedy with the firm in writing, up to and including replacing the engagement partner.
checklist.done: each breach has a dated legal assessment, a notification decision with reasoning and a written remedy agreed with the firm.

checklist.step: Disclose auditor fees and independence in the governance reporting
actions: Provide the audit fee, audit-related fee and non-audit fee split for the statutory accounts note, agreed to the ledger extract used for the cap test.
Provide the Audit Committee with the wording for the SFCR system-of-governance section describing the external audit arrangements.
Confirm the same fee figures are used in the accounts note, the cap calculation and the committee report — one number, one source.
Have the Chief Financial Officer approve the disclosure before it is published.
checklist.done: one reconciled fee split feeds the accounts note, the cap test and the governance disclosure, approved by the CFO.

checklist.step: Report the annual independence conclusion to the board
actions: Prepare the annual independence report: rotation clocks, independence letters, pre-approval register summary, fee cap ratio and any breach with its treatment.
Table it at the Audit Committee, obtain a written conclusion on the auditor's independence and effectiveness, and take that conclusion to the board.
Record the board's decision on re-appointment or tender in the minutes.
Store the report and the minute extract in the board portal against the engagement year.
checklist.done: a board-minuted independence and effectiveness conclusion exists for the engagement year.

checklist.step: Archive the engagement independence file
actions: Move the independence letters, pre-approval register, fee cap workings, rotation registers, tender file and the Art. 11 additional report into the evidence repository under the engagement year.
Apply a 10-year retention label running from the end of the engagement.
Confirm the index makes the file searchable by entity, audit firm, partner name and financial year.
Send the reference to the Chief Audit Executive for the independent test.
checklist.done: the engagement independence file is archived with a 10-year label and is searchable by entity, firm, partner and year.

testing.step: Build the population of auditor engagements and fees
actions: Extract every accounts payable invoice and open purchase order raised against the audit firm and its network firms for the year, across all group entities.
Add engagements paid by a subsidiary but managed centrally, and any service delivered without a purchase order, by searching vendor names in the network firm list.
Reconcile the extract total to the fee split disclosed in the statutory accounts note and clear every difference.
Sign the population as complete with the extraction date and query recorded.
testing.done: the engagement population reconciles to the disclosed fee note and is signed complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every engagement to a prior pre-approval
actions: Match each population row to a pre-approval register entry on service, entity and fee.
Check the approval date pre-dates the earliest invoice or work commencement date on the engagement.
List unmatched engagements and retrospective approvals as automatic exceptions with no materiality filter.
Confirm chair-only approvals sit within the delegated threshold and were reported to the next full committee.
testing.done: every engagement matches a pre-approval that pre-dates the work, or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of non-audit engagements
actions: Take 100% of engagements above the pre-approval delegated threshold and 100% of tax and valuation-adjacent services.
Take 15 further engagements by seeded random selection from the remainder, minimum 30 engagements in total.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Have the Audit Committee chair note the sampling plan.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all higher-risk service types and is noted by the committee chair.

testing.step: Re-perform the prohibited-service assessment on the sample
actions: For each sampled engagement read the scope of work document, not the invoice narrative, and classify it against Art. 5(1) of Regulation (EU) 537/2014.
Apply the member state additions and derogations for the entity's jurisdiction and record which national text was used.
Reach your own conclusion before reading the pre-approval assessment, then compare — a right answer on a wrong basis is still an exception.
Capture the scope document and your classification note in the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled engagement is independently classified against the prohibited list under the correct national text.

testing.step: Recompute the 70% non-audit fee cap
actions: Rebuild the three-year average statutory audit fee for the audited entity, its parent, its controlled undertakings and the consolidated group from the ledger extract.
Divide the year's permitted non-audit fees by that average and compare to the 70% cap in Art. 4(2), excluding services required by EU or national law from the numerator.
Compare your ratio to the one reported to the Audit Committee and explain any difference by service classification.
Any breach, or any use of a competent authority exemption, is reported as a finding with the exemption evidence.
testing.done: the cap ratio is independently recomputed at every required level and reconciles to the committee-reported figure.

testing.step: Recompute the rotation clocks from the appointment records
actions: Take the general meeting appointment resolutions and the signed audit reports for the last twelve years and count consecutive years of firm engagement per undertaking.
Count key audit partner signing years from the signature pages, not from the firm's summary.
Compare to the 10-year firm limit, the 20-year tender extension and 24-year joint audit option, and the 7-year partner limit with 3-year cooling-off.
Any date passed without a tender, extension basis or partner change is a breach, not an exception.
testing.done: rotation clocks are recomputed from primary appointment and signature records and agree to the register.

testing.step: Test engagement team independence against internal records
actions: Take the engagement team list and run it against the HR joiner file for the last 24 months to find anyone hired from the audit firm.
Run the board, key function holder and senior finance lists against the audit firm alumni declarations for the Art. 22a cooling-off period.
Confirm any match carries a documented safeguard accepted by the Audit Committee.
Report an unsafeguarded match as an independence breach requiring General Counsel assessment.
testing.done: no unsafeguarded joiner or cooling-off match exists between the engagement team and company officers.

testing.step: Trace the independence letters and the Art. 11 report to dates
actions: Confirm the engagement-acceptance independence letter pre-dates the start of audit fieldwork.
Confirm the re-confirmation letter pre-dates the audit report signature date, comparing the two dates directly.
Confirm the Art. 11 additional report reached the Audit Committee before the audit opinion was signed and that the committee minuted its independence conclusion.
Capture the document dates and the minute reference in the workpaper.
testing.done: letter dates, additional report date and audit opinion date are traced and sequenced correctly with a minuted conclusion.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and notification decision
actions: Raise a governance exception per finding with the entity, engagement, the rule breached and the amount or date involved.
Assign a root cause (procurement bypass, misclassified service, rotation clock not maintained, fee cap monitored too late) and an owner with a date.
Record the General Counsel's decision on whether the audit oversight authority or the insurance supervisor must be notified, and the deadline.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has a root cause, owner, date and a recorded notification decision from the General Counsel.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare results to the zero-tolerance thresholds for prohibited services, unapproved engagements, the 70% cap and rotation dates.
Write the conclusion — compliant, compliant with exceptions, or non-compliant — with the evidence references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who took no part in engaging or approving any sampled service, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee before the re-appointment resolution is proposed and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date exists before the re-appointment resolution.
