checklist.step: Publish the annual reporting calendar and the template ownership matrix
actions: Compute per entity the submission date: financial year end plus 14 weeks for solo, plus 20 weeks for the group, and check each national competent authority has not set an earlier date.
Back-schedule the milestones — draft QRTs at week 6, board pack at week 9, audit clearance and XBRL build at week 12, submission at week 13.
Assign each template (S.02.01, S.05.01, S.06.02, S.12.01, S.17.01, S.19.01, S.22.01, S.23.01, S.25.01, S.26.x, S.28.01, S.32.01, S.36.x) a named preparer and a named reviewer.
Circulate the calendar to Finance, Actuarial, Investments and Risk and load the milestones into the close calendar with owners.
checklist.done: every entity has a computed deadline and every template has a named preparer, reviewer and dated milestone.

checklist.step: Load the EIOPA taxonomy release and the validation rule set
actions: Download the EIOPA Solvency II taxonomy release applicable to the reference date, together with the published validation rules and the list of deactivated rules.
Load it into the regulatory reporting tool and run a smoke test on the prior period's instance to confirm the tool renders the new templates.
Record which rules changed from the prior release and warn the affected template owners in writing.
Confirm the filing indicators list matches the templates the entity is required to report under its reporting exemptions.
checklist.done: the correct taxonomy release is loaded, smoke tested, and rule changes are communicated to template owners.

checklist.step: Take in the audited financial statement figures and the valuation bridge
actions: Take the locked statutory financial statements trial balance and the Solvency II economic balance sheet from the consolidation tool.
Build the bridge line by line: IFRS or local GAAP carrying value, valuation adjustment, Solvency II value, with a reason for each adjustment under Art. 75 of the Directive.
Reconcile the Solvency II side of the bridge to template S.02.01 column C0010 and clear every difference before the QRTs are drafted.
Have the Controller review and initial the bridge.
checklist.done: a line-by-line valuation bridge reconciles the audited accounts to S.02.01 with no unexplained difference.

checklist.step: Generate the annual QRT set and clear the validations
actions: Run the annual QRT generation for each entity and produce the full validation report against the EIOPA rule set.
Clear every blocking (BV) failure at source in the ledger or the actuarial feed — never by typing over the cell.
Document each non-blocking (EV) failure left open with the reason, and prepare the explanation the NCA will expect.
Circulate the validation report to the template reviewers and require a written clearance per template.
checklist.done: zero blocking validation failures remain and every open non-blocking failure carries a written explanation and reviewer clearance.

checklist.step: Cross-check the QRT set for internal consistency
actions: Tie technical provisions in S.12.01 and S.17.01 to the balance-sheet lines in S.02.01 and to the actuarial delivery pack.
Tie own funds in S.23.01 to the S.02.01 excess of assets over liabilities, adjusted for foreseeable dividends and own shares.
Tie the SCR in S.25.01 to the module detail in the S.26 series and the MCR in S.28.01 to the SCR corridor.
Tie asset totals in S.06.02 to the balance sheet and to the custodian statement, and reinsurance recoverables to S.30/S.31.
checklist.done: all cross-template ties agree and any residual difference is documented with its cause.

checklist.step: Draft the SFCR and the RSR narrative
actions: Draft the SFCR to the Art. 51 structure — business and performance, system of governance, risk profile, valuation for solvency purposes, capital management — and annex the public disclosure templates required by Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/895.
Where Directive (EU) 2025/2 applies, produce the policyholder part in plain language and the professional part separately, and check the two do not contradict each other.
Draft or update the RSR: a full report at least every three years, otherwise a summary of material changes with the reason for each.
Cross-check every quantitative statement in the narrative against the QRT cell it comes from and annotate the source on the draft.
checklist.done: SFCR and RSR drafts exist with every quantitative statement annotated to its QRT source cell.

checklist.step: Route the package through the auditor where SFCR audit applies
actions: Give the auditor the in-scope SFCR sections and templates named in the engagement letter, with the supporting workpapers, by week 10.
Work through the auditor's queries and record each adjustment proposed, accepted or declined, with the reason and the effect on own funds.
Obtain the audit clearance or the assurance report before the board approves the SFCR.
Log any unadjusted difference on the summary of uncorrected misstatements and take it to the Audit Committee.
checklist.done: audit clearance is on file, adjustments are logged and uncorrected differences are reported to the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Collect the auditor's communications for the file
actions: Obtain the auditor's additional report to the Audit Committee under Art. 11 of Regulation (EU) 537/2014 and the management letter.
Obtain the written representations letter signed by management and check the assertions match what Finance and Actuarial can actually support.
Table both at the Audit Committee, record the discussion and log every internal control deficiency raised into the ICFR deficiency register.
File the auditor communications in the board portal against the reporting reference date.
checklist.done: the additional report, management letter and representations letter are tabled, minuted and filed, with deficiencies registered.

checklist.step: Obtain board approval of the SFCR before publication
actions: Issue the board pack with the SFCR, the QRT summary, the audit clearance and the solvency ratio movement analysis at week 9.
Present the solvency position, any breach or near-breach of the SCR or MCR, and the capital management actions taken.
Obtain an explicit board resolution approving the SFCR for publication and record the minute reference on the document.
Confirm the approving board is the administrative, management or supervisory body named in the governance map for that undertaking.
checklist.done: a dated board resolution approving the SFCR exists and its minute reference is recorded on the document.

checklist.step: Build and technically validate the XBRL instance
actions: Generate the XBRL instance for the entity with the correct entity identifier (LEI), reference date, currency and taxonomy version.
Set the filing indicators to exactly the templates being reported and confirm no indicator is set for a template with no data.
Run the technical validation locally and fix every schema and dimensional error before submission.
Archive the instance file with its checksum so the submitted artefact is provably the one tested.
checklist.done: the instance passes local technical validation with correct LEI, reference date, taxonomy version and filing indicators, and is checksummed.

checklist.step: Submit to the national competent authority portal and capture the receipt
actions: Log in to the NCA reporting portal for the entity's jurisdiction with the authorised submitter credentials and open the annual Solvency II submission for the reference date.
Upload the XBRL instance plus the SFCR PDF where the portal requires it, and complete any cover declaration the portal presents.
Wait for the portal's processing result and download the acknowledgement or rejection message — a successful upload is not a successful submission.
Where the instance is rejected, correct the cause, resubmit, and record both attempts with their timestamps.
checklist.done: an accepted submission acknowledgement with a timestamp before the deadline is downloaded and filed per entity.

checklist.step: Publish the SFCR and notify the group supervisor
actions: Publish the approved SFCR on the company website in the location the supervisor expects, keeping the prior five years available.
Record the publication date and confirm it falls within the 14-week solo or 20-week group window.
Notify the group supervisor where the group SFCR is published as a single document covering solo undertakings under Art. 256(2), and confirm each affected NCA accepted that route.
Send the published link to Investor Relations and Communications so the same figures are used externally.
checklist.done: the SFCR is published inside the deadline window, its date is recorded and the single-SFCR route is evidenced where used.

checklist.step: Handle NCA queries and any resubmission
actions: Log every NCA query with its receipt date, the template and cell in question and the response deadline the NCA set.
Prepare the answer with the template owner, have the Controller review it, and send it inside the deadline.
Where a figure changes, produce a corrected instance, obtain CFO approval for the resubmission and record the reason for restatement.
Report every resubmission to the Audit Committee with its cause and the preventive action.
checklist.done: every NCA query is answered by its deadline and every resubmission carries a CFO approval and a recorded cause.

checklist.step: Run the post-submission lessons-learned review
actions: Compare actual milestone dates to the calendar and list every milestone missed with its owner.
Count blocking validation failures by template and identify the upstream data source causing the most rework.
Agree fixes with the source owners — ledger mapping, actuarial feed layout, asset data enrichment — with dates before the next quarterly cycle.
Record the outcome in the reporting procedure so the next cycle starts from the improved version.
checklist.done: missed milestones and validation failure causes are analysed with dated fixes agreed with source owners.

checklist.step: Archive the submission evidence pack
actions: File per entity the submitted instance with its checksum, the validation report, the NCA acknowledgement, the board minute extract, the signed SFCR PDF and the auditor communications.
Apply a 10-year retention label running from the reporting reference date and set the pack read-only.
Confirm the index makes the pack searchable by legal entity, LEI, reference date and template.
Send the reference to Internal Audit for the independent test.
checklist.done: a read-only, 10-year-labelled submission pack per entity is archived and searchable by LEI and reference date.

testing.step: Build the population of required annual submissions
actions: List every undertaking authorised under Solvency II in the group plus the group submission itself, taken from the licence register rather than the reporting team's list.
Add the RSR entities due a full report this cycle based on the three-year rotation record.
Reconcile the list to template S.32.01 as filed and to the NCA portal entity list for each jurisdiction.
Sign the population as complete before any testing starts.
testing.done: the submission population is built from licence records, reconciled to S.32.01 and signed complete.

testing.step: Recompute every submission deadline and compare to the receipt
actions: For each entity recompute the deadline as financial year end plus 14 weeks (solo) or plus 20 weeks (group), and check for a stricter national date.
Read the timestamp on the NCA acknowledgement and compute the days of margin or lateness.
Treat the acknowledgement timestamp, not the upload attempt, as the submission moment.
Any submission after the deadline is a fail regardless of the reason given.
testing.done: each entity's deadline is recomputed and compared to the acknowledgement timestamp with the margin recorded.

testing.step: Draw the sample of templates for substantive testing
actions: Take 100% of S.02.01, S.23.01, S.25.01 and S.28.01 for every entity.
Take five further templates per entity by seeded random selection from the remaining reported set, weighted to templates with prior-year validation failures.
Record the seed, the population and the selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Have the Chief Audit Executive approve the plan before fieldwork.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all solvency-critical templates and is approved.

testing.step: Reconcile the QRTs to the audited financial statements
actions: Take the audited statutory trial balance and re-perform the valuation bridge to S.02.01 line by line.
Test that each valuation adjustment cites an Art. 75 basis and is supported by a valuation paper, not an unexplained plug.
Investigate every unexplained difference above 0.5% of the balance-sheet line and report it as an exception.
Capture the bridge and the trial balance extract into the workpaper.
testing.done: the QRT balance sheet is independently reconciled to the audited accounts with all differences above 0.5% explained.

testing.step: Re-run the EIOPA validations against the submitted instance
actions: Take the archived instance file, verify its checksum matches the one recorded at submission, and re-run the EIOPA validation rule set for the applicable taxonomy release.
Confirm zero blocking failures and compare the open non-blocking failures to the explanation log.
Confirm the filing indicators in the instance match the templates the entity was required to report.
Any blocking failure surviving in the submitted instance is a fail, not an exception.
testing.done: the submitted instance re-validates with zero blocking failures and its checksum matches the archived record.

testing.step: Trace the board approval and publication of the SFCR
actions: Find the board resolution approving the SFCR and confirm its date precedes the publication date and the submission date.
Confirm the approving body is the AMSB recorded for that undertaking in the governance map.
Open the published SFCR on the company website and compare its figures cell by cell against the submitted instance for the disclosure templates.
Confirm the prior five years remain available on the website.
testing.done: board approval pre-dates publication, the published figures match the submitted instance and the archive requirement holds.

testing.step: Test the auditor communications and their follow-through
actions: Confirm the Art. 11 additional report, the management letter and the written representations letter are all on file for the cycle.
Trace every internal control deficiency raised by the auditor into the ICFR deficiency register with an owner and a date.
Trace every audit adjustment accepted into the submitted QRT figures and every declined adjustment onto the summary of uncorrected misstatements.
Report any deficiency raised by the auditor that never reached the register.
testing.done: all auditor communications are on file and every deficiency and adjustment is traced into the register or the QRTs.

testing.step: Test the quarterly submissions for timeliness
actions: For each quarter recompute the deadline as quarter end plus 5 weeks solo and plus 11 weeks group.
Compare each NCA acknowledgement timestamp to the recomputed deadline and record the margin.
List every resubmission in the year with its cause and check the preventive action recorded actually landed.
Any late quarterly submission is reported alongside the annual result, not netted against it.
testing.done: all four quarterly submissions per entity are proven on time or listed late with the resubmission history.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with the entity, template, reference date, what failed and the effect on the reported solvency ratio.
Assign a root cause (source data late, mapping error, taxonomy change missed, approval sequence broken, portal rejection) and an owner.
Set a remediation date before the next quarterly submission and, for late filings, record the notification made to the NCA.
Carry every open exception into the next cycle's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a root cause, owner, date, NCA notification record where relevant and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare results to the zero-tolerance thresholds for lateness, blocking validations and unapproved publication.
State the conclusion — compliant, compliant with exceptions, or non-compliant — with the evidence references behind each element.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared, reviewed or submitted no template in the cycle, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, lateness count and committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Appointed Actuary owns the calculation of technical provisions on the Solvency II economic basis — best estimate plus risk margin — for every solo undertaking and the group; escalation to the Chief Actuary

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Solvency II Directive 2009/138/EC Arts. 76-86 and 104-106 with Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Arts. 17-61, 87-89 and 172, plus the EIOPA risk-free rate technical documentation for the reference date; re-read each quarter and on any Directive (EU) 2025/2 change to the risk margin

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly and annual valuation of technical provisions: contract boundary determination, cash-flow projection, EIOPA risk-free rate curve application with volatility or matching adjustment where approved, reinsurance recoverables with counterparty default adjustment, risk margin, and the segmentation into Solvency II lines of business

In-scope systems.value: Reserving and cash-flow projection models with their assumption sets, run logs and version control; policy and claims extracts from the data warehouse as the input; results delivered to the consolidation ledger for S.12.01 and S.17.01

Compliance procedure documented.value: Technical Provisions Valuation Procedure — data acceptance, contract boundary rules, assumption setting and approval, curve loading, model run sequence, risk margin method, analysis of change, peer review and delivery to Finance

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary and reviewed by the Model Risk Manager; re-approved annually and on any methodology change, LTG measure approval or product launch changing the contract boundary

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly valuation must deliver to Finance by quarter end plus 3 weeks to meet the 5-week solo quarterly QRT deadline; annual valuation delivers by year end plus 7 weeks against the 14-week solo annual deadline; the EIOPA risk-free rate curve for the reference date is published in the first working week of the following month and must be loaded before the run

Deadline reminders configured.value: Valuation calendar tasks at reference date minus 10 days (data cut agreed), plus 5 days (curve loaded and data accepted), plus 12 days (model runs complete), plus 15 days (peer review), plus 21 days (delivery pack signed), escalating to the Chief Actuary on slippage

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Model version, input data extracts, assumption papers, curve files, run logs, analysis of change and the signed delivery pack retained 10 years from the valuation reference date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Data rejections, failed reconciliations, late assumption approvals, unapproved model overrides and post-delivery restatements are logged with cause, quantified effect on best estimate and the corrective action

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Chief Actuary approves every methodology or assumption change applied after the assumption committee date and every restatement of a delivered valuation

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All technical provision figures produced for the reference date — best estimate and risk margin, gross and ceded, by Solvency II line of business, by currency and by entity — with their supporting model runs and assumption papers

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Any line of business where the independent recalculation differs from the reported best estimate by more than 1%, or where the reported figure cannot be reproduced from the logged model version and inputs, is a fail; any use of a curve other than the published EIOPA curve for the reference date is an automatic fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is quarterly with a full annual valuation; testing runs quarterly on a reduced scope (reproduction and curve checks) and in full at the annual reference date including independent recalculation

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must be outside the reserving team and must not have set any assumption or executed any run in the tested valuation

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly and annual technical provisions validation file (reproduction evidence, recalculation workbook, curve verification, analysis of change review, exception log) in the model governance repository indexed by reference date

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Technical provisions methodology paper, assumption papers, analysis of change, validation report and the S.12.01/S.17.01 reconciliation, presentable to the supervisor within 10 business days of an Art. 35 request

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Actuary answers supervisory questions on methodology and assumptions; the Regulatory Reporting Manager owns the formal correspondence channel; material restatements go to the Audit Committee before they go to the supervisor

checklist.step: Agree the data cut and accept the valuation data
actions: Agree the extract cut-off timestamp with the Policy Administration and Claims data owners at reference date minus 10 days and record it.

Take the policy, claims, premium and expense extracts and run the Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 19 checks: record counts, sums insured, paid and incurred totals, currency codes, inception and expiry date ranges.
Reconcile the extract control totals to the general ledger premium and claims balances and clear differences with the Controller before acceptance.
Reject and re-request any extract failing a control total rather than adjusting it inside the model, and log the rejection.
checklist.done: every extract is reconciled to the ledger, passes the Art. 19 checks and is formally accepted with a dated acceptance note.

checklist.step: Load the EIOPA risk-free rate term structure for the reference date
actions: Download from EIOPA the monthly risk-free interest rate term structure for the exact reference date, for every currency the liabilities are held in.
Load the relevant variant — with or without volatility adjustment, and with the matching adjustment portfolio curve where an approval is held — and record which variant was used per portfolio.
Verify the loaded curve against the published file by checking the ultimate forward rate, the last liquid point and three spot rates at 1, 10 and 30 years.
Store the curve file with the run inputs so the valuation is reproducible.
checklist.done: the correct EIOPA curve variant per currency and portfolio is loaded, spot-checked at three tenors and archived with the run.

checklist.step: Determine contract boundaries and segmentation
actions: Apply the Art. 18 contract boundary test to each product: recognise cash flows only where the undertaking can be compelled to provide cover or cannot reprice to fully reflect the risk.
Document the boundary conclusion per product with the policy wording clause relied on and the repricing right that exists in practice.
Map each product to the Solvency II line of business in Annex I of the Delegated Regulation and record the mapping table version.
Have the Product / Filing Actuary confirm the mapping for any product launched or repriced in the period.
checklist.done: every product has a documented contract boundary with the wording clause cited and a confirmed line-of-business mapping.

checklist.step: Set and approve the valuation assumptions
actions: Run the experience analysis for mortality, morbidity, lapse, expense, claims frequency and severity, and claims inflation, and compare actual to expected for the last three periods.
Propose the assumption set with the evidence, the alternatives considered and the quantified effect on best estimate of each proposed change.
Take the pack to the assumption committee, obtain a decision per assumption and record the approver and date.
Record every expert judgement with its rationale, materiality and approver so it satisfies the documentation standard in Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 2.
checklist.done: each assumption is approved by name and date with quantified impact, and every expert judgement is documented.

checklist.step: Project the best estimate cash flows
actions: Run the projection with the accepted data, the approved assumptions and the loaded curve, producing gross best estimate cash flows by line of business and currency.

Include all expected cash flows within the contract boundary: claims, benefits, expenses (including a going-concern expense allowance and overheads per Art. 31), premiums, and future discretionary benefits where they apply.
Include an explicit allowance for events not in data and for the time value of options and guarantees where the product carries them.
Record the model version, run identifier, machine and run timestamp in the run log.
checklist.done: the gross best estimate is produced from accepted data on approved assumptions with a logged, reproducible run identifier.

checklist.step: Value reinsurance recoverables with the counterparty default adjustment
actions: Take the in-force treaty terms from the reinsurance system — quota share percentages, excess of loss attachment and limits, reinstatements, commissions and aggregate caps — for the reference date.
Project ceded cash flows on the same assumptions and the same curve as the gross projection, respecting timing differences between claim payment and recovery.
Compute the counterparty default adjustment under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 42 using the reinsurer's credit quality step and expected recovery rate.
Reconcile the resulting recoverables to the reinsurance ledger balances and explain any difference to the Reinsurance Accountant.
checklist.done: ceded best estimate and the counterparty default adjustment are computed per treaty and reconciled to the reinsurance ledger.

checklist.step: Compute the risk margin
actions: Project the SCR for non-hedgeable risks over the run-off of the obligations using the method chosen from the EIOPA hierarchy and record which level of the hierarchy was used and why.

Apply the cost-of-capital rate set in Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 39, and where Directive (EU) 2025/2 applies use the revised rate with the exponential lambda floor, recording which basis applies at the reference date.
Discount the capital charges on the risk-free curve for the reference date and allocate the risk margin to lines of business in proportion to their contribution.
Compare the risk margin to the prior period as a percentage of best estimate and explain any movement above 10%.
checklist.done: the risk margin is computed on a named hierarchy level and cost-of-capital basis, allocated to lines of business and explained against prior period.

checklist.step: Produce the analysis of change
actions: Bridge the prior reference date best estimate to the current one in ordered steps: expected run-off, new business, experience variance, assumption changes, model changes, curve movement, foreign exchange.
Quantify each step by line of business and require the steps to sum exactly to the reported movement with no residual.
Attribute every assumption and model change step to the approved change record that caused it.
Investigate and explain any single step above 5% of opening best estimate before the pack is released.
checklist.done: the analysis of change reconciles to nil residual and every step above 5% is explained and linked to an approved change.

checklist.step: Run the validation checks required by Art. 264
actions: Perform actual-versus-expected back-testing of the prior period best estimate against experience and record the deviation by line of business.
Run sensitivity tests on the key assumptions — discount rate, lapse, claims inflation, expense — and record the best estimate movement for each.
Benchmark reserve ratios and development patterns against the prior periods and, where available, market data.
Write the validation conclusion, naming any assumption where back-testing suggests a persistent bias.
checklist.done: back-testing, sensitivities and benchmarking are run and a written validation conclusion names any biased assumption.

checklist.step: Obtain independent peer review before delivery
actions: Re-perform the highest-materiality line of business on an independent basis or with a benchmark method and compare to the model result.
Check the run used the approved assumption set version and the correct curve file, by comparing file hashes in the run log.
Challenge every expert judgement above the materiality threshold and record the challenge and the response.
Record the peer review conclusion in the model governance repository with a pass, pass-with-conditions or fail.
checklist.done: a dated independent peer review conclusion exists in the repository with the assumption and curve versions verified.

checklist.step: Assemble and sign the technical provisions delivery pack
actions: Assemble the pack: best estimate and risk margin gross and net, by line of business, by currency and by entity, plus the analysis of change, the validation conclusion and the peer review outcome.
State the model version, assumption set version, curve file and data extract identifiers on the cover so Finance can prove provenance.
Sign and date the pack and hand it to the Controller against a receipt.
Refuse to sign where a peer review condition is open, and record the reason instead.
checklist.done: a signed, dated delivery pack naming model, assumption, curve and data versions is handed to Finance against a receipt.

checklist.step: Reconcile the delivered figures into the QRTs
actions: Post the delivered figures and reconcile them to S.12.01 for life and health SLT and to S.17.01 for non-life, cell by cell for each line of business.
Reconcile the technical provisions total to the S.02.01 balance sheet and the reinsurance recoverables to the asset side.
Populate S.19.01 claims development from the same underlying triangles and check consistency with the non-life best estimate.
Clear every EIOPA validation rule touching technical provisions before the instance is built.
checklist.done: delivered technical provisions tie to S.12.01, S.17.01, S.19.01 and S.02.01 with technical provision validations cleared.

checklist.step: Explain the movement to the Chief Financial Officer and the CRO
actions: Present the analysis of change and the solvency ratio effect at the quarterly reserving committee, naming the drivers by line of business.
Highlight any assumption change that reduces reserves and the evidence supporting it, so the challenge is on the record.
Record the committee's challenge and any requested rework, with an owner and a date.
Confirm the CFO and CRO accept the figures before the QRTs are finalised.
checklist.done: the reserving committee has challenged the movement and the CFO and CRO acceptance is minuted.

checklist.step: Handle any post-delivery restatement
actions: Where an error is found after delivery, quantify the effect on best estimate, risk margin, own funds and the SCR ratio before anything else.
Obtain Chief Actuary approval for the restatement and agree with the Regulatory Reporting Manager whether a resubmission to the NCA is required.
Record the error, its cause and the control that should have caught it in the model governance repository.
Add the missing control to the valuation procedure before the next reference date.
checklist.done: every restatement is quantified, approved, reported to the reporting team and closed with a new control in the procedure.

checklist.step: Archive the valuation evidence for the reference date
actions: Archive the input extracts, curve files, assumption papers, model version, run logs, analysis of change, validation and peer review, and the signed delivery pack.
Apply the 10-year retention label from the valuation reference date and set the archive read-only.
Confirm the archive is indexed by entity, reference date, line of business and model version.
Run a reproduction spot check by re-executing one archived run and confirming it returns the delivered figure.
checklist.done: the valuation archive is read-only, labelled for 10 years and proven reproducible by a spot-check re-run.

testing.step: Build the population of reported technical provision figures
actions: Extract from the submitted QRT instance every technical provision cell in S.12.01 and S.17.01 by entity, line of business and currency, gross and ceded.
Extract independently the delivery pack figures from the model governance repository archive.
Reconcile the two extracts cell by cell and list every difference before testing starts.
Sign the population as complete with the extraction date recorded.
testing.done: the reported and delivered figures reconcile cell by cell and the population is signed complete.

testing.step: Prove the reported figure is reproducible from the archive
actions: Take the archived model version, assumption set and data extract identifiers from the run log and re-execute the run for two lines of business.
Compare the re-run output to the delivered best estimate to the cent and investigate any difference.
Verify file hashes of the assumption file and the curve file match those recorded at delivery.
Any figure that cannot be reproduced from the archive is an automatic fail.
testing.done: two lines of business are re-executed from the archive and reproduce the delivered figure with matching file hashes.

testing.step: Verify the EIOPA curve actually used
actions: Download the published EIOPA risk-free rate term structure for the reference date independently of the reserving team.
Compare the ultimate forward rate, last liquid point and spot rates at 1, 5, 10, 20 and 30 years to the curve file used in the run, for every currency.
Confirm the volatility adjustment or matching adjustment variant used matches the approval actually held, and check the approval letter date.
Any curve mismatch or unapproved LTG measure use is an automatic fail.
testing.done: the run curve matches the published EIOPA curve at all tested tenors and the LTG variant matches a held approval.

testing.step: Independently recalculate the largest line of business
actions: Rebuild the paid and incurred triangles for the largest non-life line from the claims extract and apply an independent method — chain ladder plus Bornhuetter-Ferguson — to derive an undiscounted ultimate.
Discount on the verified EIOPA curve and add the expense allowance to reach an independent best estimate.
Compare to the reported best estimate and report any difference above 1% as a fail with the driver identified.
Attach the triangles, the method workbook and the comparison to the workpaper.
testing.done: the largest line is independently recalculated and agrees within 1% or the driver of the difference is identified.

testing.step: Test the contract boundary conclusions on a sample
actions: Select eight products weighted to those launched or repriced in the period.
Read the actual policy wording and test the Art. 18 conclusion yourself: is there an unconditional repricing right, and is it exercisable in practice?
Compare the recognised future premium cash flows to the boundary conclusion — a boundary of nil with projected future premiums is a contradiction.
Report any boundary conclusion supported only by prior-year practice.
testing.done: eight product boundaries are independently re-tested against policy wording with contradictions reported.

testing.step: Recompute the risk margin
actions: Rebuild the projected non-hedgeable SCR run-off pattern using the method level the reserving team recorded and test it against the EIOPA hierarchy conditions for that level.
Apply the cost-of-capital rate in force at the reference date and discount on the verified curve.
Compare to the reported risk margin and report any difference above 2% with the driver.
Confirm the allocation across lines of business sums exactly to the reported total.
testing.done: the risk margin is independently recomputed within 2% with the hierarchy level justified and the allocation summing exactly.

testing.step: Test reinsurance recoverables and the counterparty default adjustment
actions: Select five treaties and confirm the quota share percentages, attachment points, limits and reinstatements used in the model match the signed treaty wording in the repository.
Recompute the counterparty default adjustment under Art. 42 from the reinsurer credit quality step and compare to the booked adjustment.
Reconcile the ceded best estimate to the reinsurance ledger balances and confirm timing differences are explained, not netted.
Report any treaty modelled on terms that differ from the signed wording as a fail.
testing.done: five treaties are traced to signed wording, the default adjustment is recomputed and ceded amounts reconcile to the ledger.

testing.step: Re-perform data acceptance and the analysis of change
actions: Re-run the policy and claims extracts at the recorded cut-off timestamp and compare record counts and control totals to the accepted extracts.
Confirm the extract cut-off is on or before the reference date and that no later movement was pulled in.
Re-add the analysis of change steps and confirm they sum exactly to the movement with no residual line.
Test that every assumption-change step ties to an assumption committee decision dated before the run.
testing.done: extract control totals reproduce, the cut-off holds and the analysis of change sums to nil residual with dated approvals.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, quantified effect and owner
actions: Raise an exception per finding stating the entity, line of business, the amount of the difference and its effect on own funds and the SCR ratio.
Assign a root cause (unaccepted data, wrong curve variant, boundary misapplied, assumption applied without approval, run not reproducible) and an owner.
Set the remediation date before the next quarterly reference date and require the fix to be evidenced by a re-run.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception carries a quantified effect, root cause, owner, dated fix and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the reserving committee
actions: Compare results to the 1% recalculation threshold, the 2% risk margin threshold and the zero-tolerance reproduction and curve tests.
State the conclusion — reliable, reliable with exceptions, or unreliable — with the evidence references behind each element.
Have the independent reviewer, who set no assumption and executed no run in the tested valuation, sign the validation report.
Report to the reserving committee before the QRTs are finalised and file the validation file in the model governance repository.
testing.done: a signed validation report with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the reserving committee before QRT finalisation.

checklist.step: Capture the reinsurance programme as it stands at the reference date
actions: Extract the in-force treaty schedule at the reference date: treaty name, type (quota share, surplus, excess of loss, stop loss), retention, limit, reinstatements, aggregate deductible, commission and inception/expiry.
Add facultative placements above the automatic capacity and any loss portfolio transfer or adverse development cover.
Record for each participating reinsurer its share, its credit rating and its collateral or funds-withheld position.
Reconcile the schedule to the signed slips in the treaty repository and clear any difference with the Reinsurance Manager before use.
checklist.done: the treaty schedule at the reference date is complete, reconciled to signed slips and shows reinsurer shares and ratings.

checklist.step: Assemble the gross and net loss distributions
actions: Produce the modelled gross and net aggregate loss distributions for the coming underwriting year at the 1-in-10, 1-in-50, 1-in-100 and 1-in-200 return periods.
Produce the per-risk and per-event distributions for the catastrophe-exposed lines using the catastrophe model output.
Compute the reinsurance recovery at each return period and the resulting net retained loss.
Record the model version and parameterisation so the opinion can cite it precisely.
checklist.done: gross and net loss distributions with recoveries at four return periods are produced from a cited model version.

checklist.step: Test the programme against risk appetite and capital
actions: Take the board-approved risk appetite statement and read off the limits: maximum net retained loss, minimum solvency ratio after a 1-in-200 event, maximum earnings volatility.
Compare the modelled net retained loss at each return period to those limits and record the headroom or the breach.
Compute the SCR relief the programme provides by re-running the SCR gross of reinsurance and taking the difference.
Name explicitly any scenario where the programme leaves the undertaking outside appetite.
checklist.done: net retention at each return period is compared to appetite limits and the SCR relief is quantified.

checklist.step: Test the programme for structural gaps
actions: Check for vertical gaps: any layer with unplaced capacity, and the co-reinsurance share the undertaking retains.
Check for horizontal gaps: exhaustion of reinstatements after two or three events, and aggregate cover erosion.
Check for wording gaps: hours clauses, occurrence definitions, exclusions (cyber, communicable disease, terrorism, sanctions) that could leave a modelled loss uncovered.
Check inuring order between treaties and confirm the model applies them in the contractual sequence.
checklist.done: vertical, horizontal, wording and inuring-order gaps are each tested and quantified or ruled out in writing.

checklist.step: Assess counterparty credit quality and concentration
actions: List the total recoverable exposure by reinsurer across all treaties and compare it to the internal security limit per credit quality step.
Compute the concentration: share of the programme placed with the largest three reinsurers and with any single group.
Confirm collateral, letters of credit or funds withheld are in place where the reinsurer falls below the required rating, and check expiry dates.
Feed the exposure by credit quality step into the counterparty default risk module and confirm the numbers agree with S.31.01.
checklist.done: recoverable exposure by reinsurer and credit quality step is quantified, collateral verified and reconciled to S.31.01.

checklist.step: Assess the underwriting policy for the Art. 48(1)(g) opinion
actions: Extract from the underwriting platform the written premium, technical price and achieved price by line of business and segment for the year.
Compute the rate adequacy — achieved price against technical price — and the loss ratio on an accident-year basis, and compare to plan.
Test the sufficiency of premiums to cover future claims and expenses on the current assumption set, allowing for claims inflation.
Identify the segments where new business is written below technical price and quantify the value destroyed.
checklist.done: rate adequacy and premium sufficiency are quantified by segment with below-technical-price business identified.

checklist.step: Assess sustainability risks in the underwriting opinion
actions: Identify the sustainability factors material to the portfolio: physical climate risk in property lines, transition risk in liability and motor, and social or governance factors in casualty.
Quantify the effect on expected claims of the physical risk scenario used in the ORSA and record the assumption source.
Confirm underwriting guidelines already reflect the exclusions or loadings implied, and list where they do not.
Provide the Appointed Actuary with a written input naming the factors considered, so the opinion satisfies Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 272(6a).
checklist.done: a written sustainability input naming the factors, the quantified effect and the guideline gaps is delivered to the Appointed Actuary.

checklist.step: State the reliability of technical provisions in the report
actions: Summarise the technical provisions methodology, the assumption changes in the year and the analysis of change, drawing on the signed delivery pack.
State the data quality conclusion under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 19, naming any deficiency and its quantified effect.
State the validation outcome, including back-testing deviations and the sensitivities run.
Express the reliability conclusion in plain terms and qualify it where a deficiency is unresolved.
checklist.done: the report states methodology, data quality, validation and an explicit reliability conclusion with any qualification.

checklist.step: Draft the report to the Art. 272 section structure
actions: Draft each required section: coordination of technical provisions, sufficiency of data, comparison of best estimates against experience, opinion on overall underwriting policy, opinion on adequacy of reinsurance arrangements, and contribution to the risk management system and the ORSA.
Write each opinion as a conclusion followed by its basis and its limitations — never a description of the process alone.
State any material uncertainty and the range around the central estimate where one exists.
List the recommendations with an owner suggested for each.
checklist.done: a full draft exists covering every Art. 272 section, each opinion stated as a conclusion with basis and limitations.

checklist.step: Peer review the draft before signature
actions: Check every figure quoted in the draft against its source: treaty schedule, model output, delivery pack, underwriting extract.
Challenge each conclusion for whether the evidence presented actually supports it, and require rewording where it does not.
Confirm the sustainability content is specific to this portfolio and not generic language.
Record the review comments and the author's responses so the challenge is evidenced.
checklist.done: a documented peer review with challenges and responses is complete and every quoted figure is traced to source.

checklist.step: Sign the opinion and record the signing basis
actions: Sign the report with name, professional qualification, date and the reference date it speaks to.
State the reliances placed on others — Finance for the ledger, Reinsurance for the treaty schedule, Risk for the appetite statement — and name them.
State the professional standards applied alongside the Solvency II requirements.
Refuse to sign where a peer review comment is unresolved and record the reason instead of signing.
checklist.done: the report is signed with qualification, date, reference date, named reliances and stated standards.

checklist.step: Deliver the report to the AMSB and obtain its challenge
actions: Publish the signed report to the board portal at least five business days before the board or risk committee sitting.
Ensure the Appointed Actuary presents in person and takes questions on the reinsurance and underwriting opinions.
Record in the minutes the board's challenge, its acceptance or rejection of each recommendation, and the actions arising.
Confirm the delivery date precedes the board's approval of the SFCR.
checklist.done: the report is delivered, presented and minuted with recorded challenge, before SFCR approval.

checklist.step: Turn recommendations into owned actions
actions: Raise an action per recommendation with an owner, a date and the risk register entry it mitigates.
For any reinsurance inadequacy, require the Head of Reinsurance to state whether the gap will be closed at the next renewal or accepted, and record the capital effect of acceptance.
For any underwriting profitability finding, require the Chief Underwriting Officer to state the rate or appetite change and its effective date.
Report progress to the Risk Committee quarterly until every action is closed.
checklist.done: every recommendation has an owner, a date, a risk register link and a quarterly reporting commitment.

checklist.step: Feed the opinion into the SFCR and RSR narrative
actions: Take the reinsurance adequacy conclusion into the SFCR risk profile section on risk mitigation techniques.
Take the underwriting opinion conclusion into the business and performance section and check it does not contradict the reported loss ratios.
Where the opinion is qualified, agree the disclosure wording with the Chief Actuary and the General Counsel before publication.
Cite the report date in the RSR so the supervisor can request it directly.
checklist.done: SFCR and RSR narrative reflect the opinion conclusions, with qualification wording agreed before publication.

checklist.step: Archive the opinion file
actions: Archive the signed report, the treaty schedule used, the model outputs, the underwriting extracts, the sustainability input, the peer review notes and the board minute extract.
Apply a 10-year retention label running from the report date and set the file read-only.
Confirm the index makes the file searchable by entity, report year and reference date.
Send the reference to Internal Audit for the independent review.
checklist.done: the opinion file is archived read-only with a 10-year label and is searchable by entity and report year.

testing.step: Build the section completeness matrix for the report
actions: List every task required of the actuarial function by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 272 and Directive Art. 48(1)(a)-(i) as rows.
Map each row to the page and paragraph of the signed report that discharges it.
Mark as a fail any row with no mapping, and any row where the text describes activity without stating a conclusion.
Sign the matrix as the test population for the section testing.
testing.done: every Art. 272 and Art. 48 task maps to a stated conclusion in the report or is marked failed.

testing.step: Trace every quoted figure in the report to its source record
actions: List every number appearing in the report: retentions, limits, return-period losses, SCR relief, loss ratios, rate adequacy, best estimate movements.
Trace each to its source — treaty schedule, capital model output, underwriting extract or the signed technical provisions delivery pack.
Flag any figure whose source has since been restated, and check whether the report was updated.
Any figure that cannot be traced is a fail regardless of its size.
testing.done: every quoted figure is traced to a named source record or reported as untraceable.

testing.step: Test treaty coverage completeness against the signed slips
actions: Extract every treaty and facultative placement in force at the reference date directly from the treaty repository's signed slips.
Match each to the schedule the opinion relied on and list any placement the opinion never considered.
Verify retention, limit and reinstatement figures on five treaties against the slip wording, not the system summary.
Any material treaty in force but absent from the opinion is an automatic fail.
testing.done: the opinion's treaty schedule is proven complete against signed slips with five treaties verified to wording.

testing.step: Re-perform the adequacy conclusion against risk appetite
actions: Take the board-approved risk appetite statement in force at the reference date and read the net retention and post-event solvency limits.
Recompute the net retained loss at the 1-in-200 return period from the modelled gross loss and the treaty structure, applying inuring order yourself.
Reach your own adequacy conclusion before reading the opinion's, then compare — a right conclusion on the wrong appetite version is an exception.
Confirm any breach of appetite named in the opinion reached the risk register.
testing.done: net retention at the 1-in-200 is independently recomputed and the adequacy conclusion is independently reached and compared.

testing.step: Test the counterparty credit and concentration analysis
actions: Rebuild total recoverable exposure by reinsurer from the ceded ledger and compare to the figures in the opinion.
Recompute the share held by the largest three reinsurers and compare to the internal concentration limit.
Verify collateral and letters of credit exist, are unexpired at the reference date and cover the exposure they are claimed to cover.
Reconcile the exposure by credit quality step to template S.31.01 as filed.
testing.done: recoverable exposure, concentration and collateral are independently rebuilt and reconcile to S.31.01.

testing.step: Test the sustainability content for specificity and evidence
actions: Check the opinion names the sustainability factors material to this portfolio and quantifies at least one effect on expected claims.
Trace the quantified effect to the ORSA climate scenario or the catastrophe model run cited, and confirm the run exists and is dated.
Test whether the underwriting guideline gaps listed in the opinion were raised as actions.
Generic language with no portfolio-specific factor or figure fails the Art. 272(6a) requirement.
testing.done: sustainability content names portfolio-specific factors, ties to a dated scenario run and produced tracked actions.

testing.step: Test the underwriting profitability analysis behind the opinion
actions: Re-extract written premium, technical price and achieved price by segment from the underwriting platform for the same period.
Recompute rate adequacy and the accident-year loss ratio and compare to the figures in the opinion.
Confirm the segments identified as below technical price match your own recomputation, and report any omitted segment.
Differences above 2 percentage points on rate adequacy are exceptions requiring explanation.
testing.done: rate adequacy and loss ratios are independently recomputed and agree within 2 percentage points or are explained.

testing.step: Trace signature, delivery and board challenge
actions: Confirm the signature carries the actuary's name, qualification, signing date and the reference date, and that reliances on others are named.
Compare the board portal publication date to the sitting date and confirm at least five business days of notice.
Read the minute and confirm it records substantive challenge and a decision on each recommendation, not simply that the report was noted.
Confirm the delivery date precedes the board resolution approving the SFCR.
testing.done: signature completeness, notice period, minuted challenge and pre-SFCR delivery are all evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an exception per finding naming the section, the figure or the omission and its effect on the reliability of the opinion.
Assign a root cause (stale treaty schedule, untraceable figure, generic sustainability text, activity described instead of a conclusion, late delivery) and an owner.
Set a remediation date ahead of the next annual report and require the procedure to be amended where the cause is structural.
Carry every open exception into the next annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has a root cause, owner, remediation date and, where structural, an amended procedure.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare results to the zero-tolerance tests: missing Art. 272 section, untraceable figure, uncovered material treaty, delivery after SFCR approval.
State the conclusion — the opinion is soundly based, soundly based with exceptions, or not soundly based — with the evidence references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who contributed no analysis to the report, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Risk Committee and the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and dual committee reporting is filed in the repository.
