checklist.step: Confirm what each supervisor requires and by when
actions: For each authorised undertaking read the NCA's current annual reporting instructions and note whether the Actuarial Function Report is required as a standalone document, as an RSR annex, or only on request.
Record the accepted file formats, naming convention, size limits, language and whether a signed PDF or a wet-ink scan is required.
Compute the deadline as financial year end plus 14 weeks solo or plus 20 weeks group, and check for a stricter national date.
Publish a one-page requirement sheet per jurisdiction to the reporting team and to the Chief Actuary.
checklist.done: a per-jurisdiction requirement sheet exists naming the documents, format, language and computed deadline.

checklist.step: Maintain the RSR three-year rotation register
actions: Record for each undertaking the reference date of its last full RSR and compute the next full-report year on the three-year cycle.
For intervening years record that only a summary of material changes is due, with the reason for each change described.
Check whether the supervisor has requested a full RSR out of cycle and record that request with its date.
Set a calendar alert six months before each entity's full-report year so drafting capacity is planned.
checklist.done: every undertaking shows its last full RSR date, its next full-report year and any out-of-cycle supervisory request.

checklist.step: Take delivery of the signed actuarial report and its minute
actions: Download from the board portal the signed Actuarial Function Report and the AMSB minute recording its receipt and challenge.
Verify the signature block carries the actuary's name, qualification, signing date and the reference date it speaks to.
Compute a checksum of the signed PDF and record it, so the submitted file can later be proven identical to the approved one.
Reject an unsigned draft or a version with tracked changes and go back to the Appointed Actuary.
checklist.done: the signed report and the AMSB minute are on file with a recorded checksum and a verified signature block.

checklist.step: Assemble the submission package per undertaking
actions: Build the package to the requirement sheet: annual QRT XBRL instance, RSR (full or summary), the signed Actuarial Function Report with the Art. 48(1)(g) and (h) opinions, the SFCR, and any national annex.
Name every file to the NCA convention, typically LEI, reference date, document code and version.
Run the completeness matrix — one row per required document, ticked against the actual file — and refuse to submit on a partial tick.
Store the assembled package in the regulatory reporting tool under the reference date.
checklist.done: the package is assembled, named to convention and every required document is ticked on the completeness matrix.

checklist.step: Apply the group and cross-border reporting arrangements
actions: Confirm which reports are submitted to the group supervisor and which to each solo NCA, and whether a single group RSR under Art. 256 covers subsidiaries.
Where a single document route is used, confirm each affected NCA has agreed it in writing and file that agreement with the package.
For third-country subsidiaries record the local equivalent report and its own deadline so nothing is missed outside the EU perimeter.
Circulate the routing map to the local finance leads so no entity assumes the group filed on its behalf.
checklist.done: a routing map states, per undertaking and per document, which supervisor receives it and on what agreed basis.

checklist.step: Draft the covering letter
actions: State the undertaking, LEI, reference date and the list of documents enclosed.
Note explicitly any qualification in the actuarial opinion and the management response, rather than leaving the supervisor to find it.
Note any restatement of previously submitted figures and its cause.
Have the Chief Actuary and the Chief Financial Officer clear the letter before it goes.
checklist.done: a cleared covering letter lists the enclosures and flags every qualification and restatement.

checklist.step: Check submitter credentials and portal access ahead of the window
actions: Confirm the authorised submitter for each NCA portal is a current employee with valid credentials and, where required, a valid certificate or token.
Test login on each portal at least two weeks before the deadline and record the test date.
Confirm a named backup submitter exists per jurisdiction and has tested access as well.
Raise an access request immediately where a credential has expired — never on submission day.
checklist.done: primary and backup submitter access is tested per portal at least two weeks before the deadline.

checklist.step: Submit the package and capture the receipt
actions: Log in to the NCA portal, open the annual submission for the undertaking and the reference date, and upload each document to its designated slot.
Complete the portal declaration and submit, then wait for the processing outcome rather than closing at upload.
Download the acknowledgement or rejection message with its timestamp and reference number.
Where rejected, fix the cause, resubmit, and record both attempts with their timestamps and the reason.
checklist.done: an accepted acknowledgement with a timestamp before the deadline is downloaded for every undertaking.

checklist.step: Prove the submitted report equals the approved report
actions: Recompute the checksum of the file actually uploaded and compare it to the checksum recorded at board approval.
Where they differ, identify what changed and whether the change was authorised by the Appointed Actuary in writing.
Record the checksum comparison on the submission record as the provenance evidence.
Treat any unauthorised difference as a reportable control failure, not a formatting matter.
checklist.done: the uploaded file checksum matches the board-approved version or the difference is authorised in writing.

checklist.step: Log the submission against the obligation register
actions: Update the regulatory obligation register with the submission date, the acknowledgement reference and the days of margin against the deadline.
Attach the acknowledgement and the completeness matrix to the obligation record.
Close the obligation only on an acknowledgement, never on an upload confirmation.
Roll the obligation forward with next year's computed deadline.
checklist.done: the obligation register records the acknowledgement reference, margin and attachments, and is rolled forward.

checklist.step: Handle supervisory follow-up on the actuarial opinion
actions: Log every NCA query with its receipt date, the document and section in question, and the response deadline the supervisor set.
Route technical questions on reserves, reinsurance adequacy or sustainability to the Chief Actuary and hold the drafted answer for CFO clearance.
Send the response inside the deadline and file the sent copy with the query.
Where the query implies a deficiency, open an action with an owner before the response is sent.
checklist.done: every supervisory query is logged, answered inside its deadline and, where it implies a deficiency, has an owned action.

checklist.step: Manage any resubmission or late notification
actions: Where a document was omitted or a figure changed, decide with the Chief Actuary whether a resubmission or an addendum is required.
Approve the notification to the NCA, stating what was wrong, the corrected position and the preventive action.
Notify the Audit Committee of every late filing or resubmission at its next sitting.
Record the CFO approval and the notification date on the submission record.
checklist.done: every resubmission or late filing has CFO approval, an NCA notification and an Audit Committee report.

checklist.step: Run the post-submission review
actions: Compare actual submission dates to the deadlines and list every entity with less than five days of margin.
List the causes of any rejection or resubmission by document type and identify the upstream owner.
Agree fixes with those owners with dates ahead of the next annual cycle, and amend the requirement sheets where an NCA changed its instructions mid-cycle.
Record the outcome in the submission procedure.
checklist.done: thin-margin entities and rejection causes are analysed with dated fixes agreed with upstream owners.

checklist.step: Report the submission status to the Audit Committee
actions: Prepare a status page per undertaking: deadline, submission date, margin, acknowledgement reference, open supervisory queries.
Highlight any late filing, resubmission or open query with a due date inside the next quarter.
Table it at the Audit Committee and record the minute reference.
Publish the status page to the board portal for the record.
checklist.done: a per-entity submission status page is tabled and minuted at the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Archive the submission evidence
actions: File per undertaking the submitted package, the completeness matrix, the covering letter, the acknowledgement, the checksum comparison and any supervisory correspondence.
Apply a 10-year retention label from the reporting reference date and set the pack read-only.
Confirm the index makes the pack searchable by entity, LEI, reference date and document type.
Send the reference to the Compliance Officer for the independent test.
checklist.done: a read-only, 10-year-labelled submission pack per undertaking is archived and searchable by LEI and reference date.

testing.step: Build the population of required actuarial submissions
actions: Take the list of authorised undertakings from the licence register and the group entity, independently of the reporting team's list.
Add each entity's RSR rotation status to determine whether a full report or a summary was due this cycle.
Reconcile the list to the S.32.01 entity list and to the NCA portal entity lists per jurisdiction.
Sign the population as complete before testing starts.
testing.done: the submission population is built from licence records, includes RSR rotation status and is signed complete.

testing.step: Recompute deadlines and compare to acknowledgement timestamps
actions: Recompute each deadline as financial year end plus 14 weeks solo or plus 20 weeks group and check for a stricter national date on the requirement sheet.
Read the acknowledgement timestamp for each entity and compute the margin or the lateness in days.
Treat the acknowledgement, not the upload attempt, as the submission moment.
Any late submission is a fail regardless of the explanation.
testing.done: each deadline is recomputed and compared to the acknowledgement timestamp with the margin recorded.

testing.step: Test package completeness against the supervisor's own instructions
actions: Obtain each NCA's published annual reporting instructions directly, not the internal requirement sheet.
Build your own required-document list and compare it to the documents actually submitted.
Confirm the Actuarial Function Report and both Art. 48(1)(g) and (h) opinions are present where required, and the national annexes too.
Any missing required document is a fail even where the supervisor has not complained.
testing.done: the submitted package is tested against the supervisor's own published instructions with omissions listed.

testing.step: Prove the submitted report is the AMSB-approved version
actions: Take the signed report from the board portal and recompute its checksum.
Recompute the checksum of the file retrieved from the archived submission pack and compare the two.
Where they differ, open both files and identify the changed content and whether the Appointed Actuary authorised it in writing.
Confirm the AMSB minute date precedes the submission date.
testing.done: the submitted and approved files are checksum-matched, or the difference is identified and shown to be authorised.

testing.step: Test the group and cross-border routing
actions: Take the routing map and confirm every undertaking received a submission from someone — group or solo — with no entity relying on an assumption.
Where a single group document covered a subsidiary under Art. 256, find the written agreement from that subsidiary's NCA and check it is current.
For third-country subsidiaries confirm the local equivalent report was filed by its own deadline.
Report any entity with no evidenced submission route as a fail.
testing.done: every undertaking has an evidenced submission route with written NCA agreement where a single document was used.

testing.step: Test the RSR three-year rotation register
actions: Rebuild each undertaking's full-RSR history from the archived submission packs of the last four years.
Confirm no entity has gone more than three years without a full RSR, and that intervening years carried a summary of material changes.
Check any out-of-cycle supervisory request for a full RSR was met by its stated deadline.
Any entity beyond the three-year cycle is a fail.
testing.done: the rotation register is rebuilt from archived packs and no entity exceeds the three-year full-RSR cycle.

testing.step: Trace supervisory queries to timely, cleared responses
actions: List every NCA query received in the cycle with its receipt date and stated response deadline.
Trace each to the sent response and compute whether it landed inside the deadline.
Confirm technical answers carry Chief Actuary input and CFO clearance where the response conceded a deficiency.
Confirm every query implying a deficiency produced an owned action with a date.
testing.done: every query traces to a timely, cleared response and any implied deficiency has an owned action.

testing.step: Test portal access controls and submitter authorisation
actions: List the individuals holding NCA portal submitter credentials per jurisdiction and compare to the authorised submitter list in the procedure.
Check every credential holder is a current employee in the reporting function and that leavers were removed within the access removal standard.
Confirm a tested backup submitter exists per jurisdiction and that the access test was performed before the filing window.
Report any active credential held by a leaver as a control failure requiring immediate revocation.
testing.done: portal credentials reconcile to the authorised list with no leaver access and a tested backup per jurisdiction.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the entity, the document, the deadline and what failed.
Assign a root cause (requirement sheet stale, package assembled late, credential expired, version control failure, routing assumption) and an owner.
Set a remediation date before the next annual cycle and record any NCA notification made.
Carry every open exception into the next cycle's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has a root cause, owner, date, notification record and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare results to the zero-tolerance thresholds for lateness, missing documents and version mismatch.
State the conclusion — compliant, compliant with exceptions, or non-compliant — with the evidence references behind each element.
Have the independent reviewer, who assembled and submitted no package in the cycle, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, lateness count and committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: ALM Actuary maintains the written asset-liability management policy and the cash-flow matching evidence required by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 260(1)(b); escalation to the Chief Risk Officer and the Chief Investment Officer

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Arts. 18, 44, 259 and 260(1)(b) with Solvency II Directive 2009/138/EC Arts. 44, 77b and 77c on the matching adjustment and Art. 132 on the prudent person principle; re-read annually and on any matching adjustment application

In-scope processes.value: Asset-liability management cycle: liability cash-flow projection, asset cash-flow projection, duration and convexity measurement, cash-flow matching and gap analysis, liquidity stress, matching adjustment portfolio monitoring where approved, and the annual ALM policy review

In-scope systems.value: Investment system providing asset cash flows, durations and holdings; the actuarial platform providing liability cash flows; results consolidated into the ALM report and template S.06.02 for the asset listing

Compliance procedure documented.value: Asset-Liability Management Policy and Procedure — matching objectives and tolerances by portfolio, measurement method for duration and cash-flow gaps, shared risk driver map, stress set, breach escalation and the matching adjustment eligibility tests

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the board on the recommendation of the Risk Committee and the Investment Committee; reviewed at least annually and on any change of matching tolerance, product mix or matching adjustment approval

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: ALM measurement runs quarterly to feed the 5-week solo quarterly QRT cycle and in full annually before the 14-week SFCR date; matching adjustment portfolios are monitored continuously with a breach requiring restoration within 2 months under Art. 77b(3), and the ALM policy is re-approved by the board annually

Deadline reminders configured.value: Quarterly ALM run tasks at reference date plus 10 days (asset and liability cash flows delivered) and plus 18 days (gap report issued); annual policy review scheduled 8 weeks before the board sitting; matching adjustment breach clock alerts at day 30 and day 45 of the 2-month restoration window

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: ALM policy versions with board approval minutes, quarterly cash-flow matching reports, stress results, breach records and matching adjustment eligibility evidence retained 10 years from the measurement date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Duration or cash-flow gap breaches, liquidity shortfalls under stress, matching adjustment eligibility failures and unapproved deviations from the policy are logged with the exposure, the restoration plan and the deadline

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CIO signs off every rebalancing plan closing an ALM breach; the Chief Risk Officer confirms the plan restores the position within tolerance and within the regulatory restoration window

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All ALM-managed portfolios at the measurement date with their asset and liability cash-flow projections, duration and gap measurements, stress results, and any matching adjustment portfolio with its assigned assets

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Any portfolio outside its board-approved duration tolerance at the measurement date without a recorded breach is a fail; any cash-flow bucket gap exceeding the policy tolerance without a restoration plan is a fail; any matching adjustment portfolio breach not restored within the 2-month Art. 77b(3) window is a regulatory breach

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous with quarterly measurement; testing runs quarterly on gap reproduction and annually in full, including independent projection of liability cash flows and matching adjustment eligibility re-testing

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside both Investments and the ALM team and must not have produced any tested projection

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly and annual ALM validation file (cash-flow reproduction, duration recomputation, gap comparison, stress re-run, matching adjustment eligibility trace) in the model governance repository indexed by measurement date

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Board-approved ALM policy, quarterly matching reports, stress results and the matching adjustment eligibility file, presentable to the supervisor within 10 business days and required at any matching adjustment or volatility adjustment review

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Risk Officer fronts supervisory questions on ALM and matching adjustment compliance; the Chief Investment Officer answers on portfolio construction; the Regulatory Reporting Manager owns the formal channel and logs every interaction

checklist.step: Review and re-approve the written ALM policy
actions: Re-read the policy against Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 260(1)(b) and confirm it identifies the interdependence between assets and liabilities, the measurement of duration and cash-flow matching, and the sensitivity of both to shared risk drivers.
Update the tolerance table: duration mismatch limit per portfolio, cash-flow gap limit per maturity bucket, currency mismatch limit and liquidity coverage minimum.
Map the shared risk drivers explicitly — interest rates, inflation, credit spreads, foreign exchange, longevity and lapse behaviour — and state how each moves both sides of the balance sheet.
Take the revised policy to the Risk Committee and the Investment Committee and then to the board for approval, and record the minute reference on the document.
checklist.done: the board has approved a current ALM policy with tolerances and an explicit shared risk driver map, with a minute reference.

checklist.step: Segment the balance sheet into ALM portfolios
actions: Define the ALM portfolios — annuities in payment, with-profits, unit-linked, non-life short tail, non-life long tail, shareholder funds — and record the liabilities assigned to each.
Assign the backing assets to each portfolio in the investment system and confirm no asset is assigned twice.
Where a matching adjustment approval is held, ring-fence that portfolio and record the assignment as irrevocable under Art. 77b(1)(a).
Reconcile the sum of portfolio assets to total investments in the balance sheet and to template S.06.02.
checklist.done: every liability and every asset sits in exactly one ALM portfolio and the totals reconcile to S.06.02.

checklist.step: Project the liability cash flows for the measurement date
actions: Run the best estimate cash-flow projection by portfolio, by currency and by annual maturity bucket to the end of the run-off.
Split benefits, expenses and premiums so the net cash-flow profile is visible bucket by bucket.
Use the same approved assumption set and the same EIOPA curve as the technical provisions valuation, and record the run identifier.
Hand the projection to the ALM Actuary against a receipt, with the model version stated.
checklist.done: liability cash flows by portfolio, currency and maturity bucket are delivered from a logged run consistent with the valuation.

checklist.step: Project the asset cash flows and measure duration
actions: Extract contractual asset cash flows — coupons, redemptions, amortisation, rental income — by portfolio, currency and maturity bucket at the measurement date.
Apply the prepayment, call and extension assumptions for callable and structured holdings and record the assumption source.
Compute modified duration and convexity per portfolio on the EIOPA curve so the asset and liability measures are on the same basis.
Reconcile the asset holdings used to the custodian statement and to template S.06.02 before releasing the extract.
checklist.done: asset cash flows, duration and convexity are produced per portfolio and the holdings reconcile to the custodian and S.06.02.

checklist.step: Measure the duration and cash-flow gaps
actions: Compute the duration gap per portfolio as asset duration less liability duration, on the same curve and same currency.
Compute the net cash-flow gap per maturity bucket and cumulatively, and express each as a percentage of the liability cash flow in that bucket.
Compare every gap to the board-approved tolerance and mark each portfolio in tolerance, on watch or in breach.
Attribute the movement since the prior quarter to new business, asset trading, curve movement and assumption change.
checklist.done: duration and bucket cash-flow gaps are computed per portfolio, compared to tolerance and attributed to drivers.

checklist.step: Run the shared risk driver sensitivities
actions: Run parallel and non-parallel interest rate shocks and record the movement in assets, in technical provisions and in own funds for each.
Run credit spread, inflation and foreign exchange shocks and record the same three movements.
Test the shocks that move both sides in the same direction and those that do not — the second set is where the mismatch bites.
Compare the own funds sensitivity to the risk appetite limit and flag any shock that breaches it.
checklist.done: each shared risk driver shock is run with the asset, liability and own funds movement recorded and compared to appetite.

checklist.step: Run the liquidity stress and the liquidity coverage measure
actions: Build the 1-month, 3-month and 12-month net liquidity requirement from projected claims, surrenders, expenses, collateral calls and reinsurance recoveries.
Classify assets into liquidity tiers using observed market depth and haircut assumptions, evidenced from market data.
Compute the liquidity coverage ratio per horizon and compare to the policy minimum.
Stress it with a mass-lapse event and a catastrophe payout and record the coverage under stress.
checklist.done: liquidity coverage is computed at three horizons with tiered assets and tested under mass lapse and catastrophe stress.

checklist.step: Test matching adjustment portfolio eligibility where approved
actions: Confirm the assigned asset portfolio still meets Art. 77b(1): cash flows are fixed or fixed-with-inflation, the assignment is maintained over the life of the obligations, and the liabilities carry no future premiums.
Test the cash-flow matching quality against the tolerance in the approval and record the test result per bucket.
Confirm no asset in the portfolio has been downgraded below the credit quality allowed and that any downgraded asset was replaced within the permitted period.
Where the matching test fails, start the Art. 77b(3) clock and notify the supervisor and the Chief Risk Officer immediately — restoration is required within two months or the adjustment must cease.
checklist.done: matching adjustment eligibility is re-tested per condition, with the two-month restoration clock started and notified on any failure.

checklist.step: Test volatility adjustment use where relied on
actions: Confirm the approval to apply the volatility adjustment is in force for each portfolio relying on it.
Recompute own funds and the SCR ratio without the volatility adjustment and record the impact, as the SFCR disclosure requires.
Confirm the impact is reported in template S.22.01 on the long-term guarantee measures.
Where removing the adjustment would breach the SCR, prepare the remediation plan the supervisor will require.
checklist.done: the without-volatility-adjustment position is computed, reported in S.22.01 and any resulting breach has a remediation plan.

checklist.step: Produce the quarterly ALM report
actions: Assemble per portfolio: duration gap, bucket cash-flow gaps, sensitivity results, liquidity coverage, matching adjustment status and the tolerance comparison.
State a conclusion per portfolio — within tolerance, on watch, or in breach — with the action required for each breach.
Name the model versions, data extracts and curve used so the report is reproducible.
Issue it to the Investment Committee and the Risk Committee at the same time so neither sees it first.
checklist.done: a reproducible quarterly ALM report states a tolerance conclusion and required action per portfolio.

checklist.step: Agree the rebalancing plan for any breach
actions: For each breach agree the trades that close the gap — duration extension, swap overlay, asset switch — with the expected post-trade gap.
Test the plan for the cost, the market impact and the SCR effect of the new holdings before committing.
Set the execution deadline inside the policy restoration window, and inside the two-month window for a matching adjustment breach.
Have the Chief Risk Officer confirm the plan actually restores the position within tolerance.
checklist.done: each breach has a costed rebalancing plan with an expected post-trade gap, a deadline and CRO confirmation.

checklist.step: Track the breach to evidenced restoration
actions: Raise a breach record with the portfolio, the measure breached, the size of the breach and the restoration deadline.
Re-measure the gap after execution and attach the post-trade measurement as closure evidence.
Reject closure claimed on executed trades alone — closure requires a re-measured gap inside tolerance.
Report open breaches to the Risk Committee monthly until closed.
checklist.done: every breach closes only on a re-measured in-tolerance gap and open breaches are reported monthly.

checklist.step: Feed the ALM position into the ORSA and the SFCR
actions: Take the sensitivity and liquidity results into the ORSA as the market and liquidity risk evidence, citing the measurement date.
Draft the SFCR risk profile text on ALM and liquidity risk, including the expected profit in future premiums and the liquidity risk concentration where material.
Confirm the long-term guarantee measure impacts quoted in the narrative agree to S.22.01.
Have the Chief Risk Officer approve the wording before it goes to the board.
checklist.done: ORSA and SFCR risk profile text is drafted from the ALM results and agrees to S.22.01, approved by the CRO.

checklist.step: Review the prudent person principle compliance of the portfolio
actions: Test the portfolio against Art. 132: assets held in the whole portfolio's security, quality, liquidity and profitability, and properly diversified.
List holdings the undertaking cannot properly measure, monitor and manage and either evidence the capability or plan the exit.
Confirm derivatives are used only to reduce risk or for efficient portfolio management, with the purpose documented per trade.
Record the conclusion for the Investment Committee minute.
checklist.done: a documented prudent person assessment covers security, quality, liquidity, diversification and derivative purpose.

checklist.step: Archive the ALM evidence for the measurement date
actions: Archive the liability and asset cash-flow extracts, the gap workbook, the sensitivity and liquidity results, the matching adjustment eligibility test and the issued report.
Apply a 10-year retention label from the measurement date and set the archive read-only.
Confirm the archive is indexed by portfolio, measurement date and model version.
Send the reference to the Model Risk Manager for the independent validation.
checklist.done: the ALM archive is read-only, labelled for 10 years and indexed by portfolio, measurement date and model version.

testing.step: Build the population of ALM portfolios and assigned assets
actions: Extract the portfolio structure and asset assignments from the investment system at the measurement date, independently of the ALM team.
Extract the liability assignment from the actuarial platform and confirm every liability line sits in exactly one portfolio.
Reconcile total assigned assets to the balance sheet investments and to template S.06.02 as filed, and list any double-assigned or unassigned holding.
Sign the population as complete with the extraction date recorded.
testing.done: portfolio assignments reconcile to S.06.02 with no double-assigned or unassigned asset, and the population is signed.

testing.step: Reproduce the liability cash-flow projection
actions: Take the run identifier recorded on the ALM report and re-execute the liability projection for two portfolios.
Compare the bucketed cash flows to those used in the gap workbook, bucket by bucket.
Confirm the run used the same assumption set and EIOPA curve as the technical provisions valuation, by comparing file hashes.
Any inconsistency between the ALM projection and the valuation projection is an automatic exception.
testing.done: two liability projections are reproduced bucket by bucket and proven consistent with the valuation run.

testing.step: Recompute duration and the duration gap independently
actions: Rebuild modified duration for the largest portfolio from the asset cash flows and the EIOPA curve in a controlled workbook.
Rebuild liability duration on the same curve and compute the duration gap yourself.
Compare to the reported gap and report any difference above 0.25 years with the driver identified.
Confirm both sides were measured on the same curve and same currency — a mixed-basis gap is meaningless and is an exception.
testing.done: the duration gap for the largest portfolio is independently rebuilt and agrees within 0.25 years on a consistent basis.

testing.step: Re-perform the bucket cash-flow gap and tolerance comparison
actions: Recompute the net cash-flow gap per maturity bucket for three portfolios from the reproduced projections.
Compare each gap to the board-approved tolerance version in force at the measurement date, not the current version.
List every portfolio marked in tolerance by the report that your recomputation puts in breach.
An unreported breach is a fail; a reported breach with no restoration plan is also a fail.
testing.done: bucket gaps are recomputed for three portfolios and compared to the tolerance version in force, with unreported breaches listed.

testing.step: Re-run the shared risk driver sensitivities
actions: Re-run the parallel and non-parallel interest rate shocks and the credit spread, inflation and foreign exchange shocks on the reproduced positions.
Compare the own funds movement to the reported figures and investigate differences above 5%.
Confirm both the asset and the liability side were shocked, not the asset side alone — a one-sided sensitivity is an automatic exception.
Compare the worst-case own funds movement to the risk appetite limit and confirm any breach was escalated.
testing.done: sensitivities are re-run two-sided, agree within 5% on own funds and appetite breaches are proven escalated.

testing.step: Re-test matching adjustment eligibility condition by condition
actions: For each matching adjustment portfolio test the Art. 77b(1) conditions individually: fixed cash flows, irrevocable assignment, no future premiums, no surrender value exceeding assets, mortality risk within the 5% limit.
Sample ten assigned assets and confirm their cash flows are genuinely fixed or inflation-linked as claimed, reading the instrument terms.
Re-perform the cash-flow matching test against the tolerance in the approval letter, not an internal tolerance.
Where a breach occurred, compute the days elapsed against the two-month Art. 77b(3) restoration window and confirm the supervisor was notified.
testing.done: every matching adjustment condition is individually re-tested, ten assets verified to instrument terms and the restoration clock checked.

testing.step: Re-perform the liquidity coverage computation
actions: Rebuild the 1-month, 3-month and 12-month net liquidity requirement from the claims, surrender, expense and collateral projections.
Re-apply the liquidity tiers and haircuts using observed market data and test whether the haircuts are supportable for the least liquid tier.
Recompute the coverage ratio at each horizon and compare to the reported figure and the policy minimum.
Re-run the mass-lapse and catastrophe stress and confirm the stressed coverage was reported, not just the base case.
testing.done: liquidity coverage is recomputed at three horizons with supportable haircuts and the stressed case is proven reported.

testing.step: Test breach records to evidenced restoration
actions: List every ALM breach raised in the year with its size, deadline and closure date.
For each closed breach obtain the post-trade re-measurement and confirm it puts the gap inside tolerance.
Reject closures evidenced only by trade confirmations and reopen them as exceptions.
Compare closure dates to the policy restoration window and, for matching adjustment breaches, to the two-month regulatory window.
testing.done: every breach closure is supported by a post-trade re-measurement inside tolerance and within its restoration window.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, exposure and owner
actions: Raise an exception per finding naming the portfolio, the measure, the size of the difference and the own funds exposure it implies.
Assign a root cause (mixed measurement basis, stale tolerance version, one-sided sensitivity, unassigned asset, unsupported haircut, matching condition drift) and an owner.
Set a remediation date before the next quarterly measurement and require a re-measurement as closure evidence.
Escalate immediately any matching adjustment eligibility failure not already notified to the supervisor.
testing.done: each exception has a quantified exposure, root cause, owner, dated fix and immediate escalation where eligibility failed.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the committees
actions: Compare results to the tolerance thresholds, the 0.25-year duration recomputation threshold and the 5% sensitivity threshold.
State the conclusion — ALM controls are effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the evidence references behind each element.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Investments and the ALM team and produced no tested projection, sign the validation report.
Report to the Risk Committee and the Investment Committee before the quarterly QRTs are finalised and file the validation file in the model governance repository.
testing.done: a signed validation report with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to both committees before QRT finalisation.
